and having worshipped with water for the feet (*pādya*) and other offerings while reciting *oṃ huṃ vāgīśvaryai namaḥ*, one should contemplate Īśāna as the head and [the goddess] as being in her fertile state (*ṛtumatī*), and [perform] the rite of presence (*sannidhāna*).

One should display the *yoni-mudrā*; then, having brought fire from a sun-crystal, from a fire-drill, or even from the hearth of a *śrotriya*, one should cause that blazing fire to enter the vessel which has been covered by another vessel.
Having thus brought the blazing fire situated within the vessel...

Oṃ phaṭ! I perform the sprinkling (prokṣaṇa) of the fire, phaṭ. Likewise, I perform the gazing (nirīkṣaṇa), phaṭ. The veiling (avaguṇṭhana): Oṃ hūṃ, I veil [it], hūṃ. The veiling with the armor (kavaca): Oṃ phaṭ, I expel the flesh-eating demons (kravyāda).

Reciting "ṣkarṣayāmi phaṭ," one should ignite two blades of *darbha* grass and cast them toward the southwest, saying: "May there be purification for the flesh-eating fire, svāhā. Then, having recited the root mantra, one should grasp the fire-vessel with both hands using sesame seeds.
Having first smelled [the fire] with the tip of the tongue,

or else having caused the flame-tip to enter the heart through the nostrils by means of *pūraka* (inhalation), one unifies it with the fire of one's own consciousness and exhales it out through the right nostril by means of *recaka* (exhalation).
Having recited the root mantra, one should cast [the offering] into the vessel with "Oṃ Raṃ, obeisance to Agni.

One should perform worship with the limbs-mantras and the consecration into nectar (*amṛtīkaraṇa*) with the root mantra. Then, having assumed the identification with Śiva with firm resolve, thinking "I myself am Śiva," one should proceed.

Having meditated on the fire in the form of semen and having conceived Māyā as Vāgīśī, one should rotate [the fire] three times within the womb with the mantra: "Oṃ, salutation to the one who causes the fire to revolve in the womb. Then, with the mantra: "Oṃ hūṃ, salutation to the one who joins [it] in this womb," one should cast it into the southwest (nairṛtya) direction.

Then, having covered the womb of the Goddess with *kuśa* grass, one performs the covering of the womb with *darbha* grass while reciting: "Oṃ, for the sake of protecting the embryo, I cover the womb of Vāgīśī; obeisance. Then: "Oṃ phaṭ, I fashion the enclosure; obeisance."
With tips of *darbha* grass pointing upward, one should establish the boundary lines (*akṣavāṭa*) in the ten directions with the mantra:
*oṃ phaṭ vāgīśyāḥ kaṅkaṇaṃ badhnāmi namaḥ*.
One should then offer the *darbha* purifier (*pavitra*) while placing the bracelet (*kaṅkaṇa*) on the right hand.
One should meditate on the form [of Agni] with the mantra *oṃ rāṃ agnigarbhāyai namaḥ*; this is the worship.
Then, with three sesame seeds, one performs the impregnation (*garbhādhāna*) of Agni with: *oṃ juṃ agner garbhādhānaṃ karomi svāhā* (3); *oṃ juṃ agne garbhādhānaṃ sampādyatāṃ svāhā* (3).

Oṃ vyoṃ agne pumān bhava nam iti, with this mantra, one should sprinkle a drop of water with the tip of a *kuśa* blade as an *argha* offering. Oṃ vyoṃ agnaye puṃse namaḥ, thus is the worship. Oṃ vyoṃ agne puṃsavanaṃ karomi svāhā.

Hā! (3) May this *puṃsavana* rite be accomplished, svāhā! (3) Oṃ ī! O Agni, you whose limbs are divided, obeisance!—having thus drawn the entire body of Agni with the tips of *darbha* grass, [one offers] to the one who has the form of Agni. Oṃ ī! To Agnyākāra... [svāhā].

*Maḥ* (the syllable of worship). *Oṃ hūṃ*, I perform the visualization of the eastern face of Agni; *svāhā*. (3) May it be accomplished. (3) *Oṃ hūṃ*, I perform the visualization of the three eyes of Agni; *svāhā*. (3) May it be accomplished. (3) *Oṃ hūṃ saḥ*.
I make the face of Agni the Īśitattva; svāhā! (3) Let it be accomplished! (3) Oṃ hūṃ juṃ, I make the heart of Agni the Vidyātattva; svāhā! (3) Let it be accomplished! (3)

Oṃ oṃ, I fashion the feet of Agni from the *ātmatattva*; svāhā! (3) Let it be accomplished! (3) Oṃ ī, I restore to life the head, shoulders, hips, feet, and all the limbs of Agni; svāhā! (3) Let it be joined! (3) Oṃ.
Oṃ Īṃ, I perform the demarcation of the boundary for Agni, svāhā! (3) Samyā (3).
Oṃ Īṃ, I perform the parting of the hair for Agni, svāhā! (3) Samyā (3).
Oṃ Phaṭ, I revive Agni, svāhā! (3) Samyā (3). Oṃ Phaṭ.

Having performed the worship with "Oṃ phaṭ agne," and having made the request, "Oṃ phaṭ agne prasava abhimukho bhava," while forming the añjali gesture or visualizing that Agni has arisen from the *gī* syllable, [one recites] "Oṃ phaṭ jñāna..."

Worship with "To Agni, whose nature is power. Oṃ hūṃ, I perform the birth-rite (*jātakarman*) for Agni, svāhā. (3) Saṃpā (3) oṃ phaṭ astrāya phaṭ; may there be purification from the impurity of birth (*sūtakaśuddhi*) for Agni, svāhā. (3) Saṃpā (3) oṃ phaṭ.
I perform the opening of the mouth of Agni, svāhā (3). Saṃpā (3). Oṃ phaṭ! I perform the malevolent incantation (*abhicāra*) of the mouth of Agni, svāhā (3). Saṃpā (3). Oṃ phaṭ!
I sweep around Agni, phaṭ. Oṃ phaṭ! [I sweep around] Agni...
*Ryupañcābhiphaṭ oṃ phaṭ agniṃ pariṣiñcāmi phaṭ*. Then, the placement of the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*) and the sacrificial grass (*viṣṭara*):
three [sticks] with their tips pointing north in the east; five each with their tips pointing east in the south and the north; and [five] in the west.

One should offer the supreme and foremost weapons with the weapon-mantra (*astramantra*). Then, in the four directions, starting from the east and ending in the north, one should spread the enclosures with "Phaṭ!
I spread the enclosures, Phaṭ! and thus offer the enclosures. Above that, [one should proceed].
One should offer four oblations: in the east, *oṃ brahmaṇe namaḥ*;
in the south, *oṃ rudrāya namaḥ*; in the west, *viṣṇave namaḥ*;
and in the north, *oṃ sadāśivāya namaḥ*. Then, [one should worship] the Jvālāliṅga.
One should worship the Peace Vase (śāntikalaśa) with the *rimūla* mantra.
Regarding its visualization, it says: one should meditate upon the four-armed Lord Śīkaṇṭha, who has a blue throat, holds a trident in his four hands, and carries a rosary in his hand.
One should meditate upon the extremely fierce Lord mounted on a bull, accompanied by Śakti who is distinct from him;
in his lap, one should contemplate the Goddess, golden-hued, holding a rosary and a water-pot, with hands in the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, and having the form of light. Oṃ huṃ jvā.
"Oṃ, obeisance to Amṛteśvara Bhairava residing in Lāliṅga"—with this, perform the worship.

Thus is the worship of the Peace Vase (śāntikalaśa) with the root mantra and its limbs. Then, having gone to the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), one should worship the ten world-protectors (lokapāla) in the ten directions.

At the time of the fire oblation (homa), one should meditate upon Hari, who is mounted by Rāvaṇa, possesses a thousand eyes, holds a thunderbolt in his hand, and is joined with Svāhā. *Oṃ laṃ, obeisance to Indra, who holds a thunderbolt in his hand*, [one should worship him] in the east. He has five faces and wide eyes, and is accompanied by Svāhā.

One should always meditate upon him as being accompanied [by his consort], mounted on a parrot, holding a spear in his hand, and possessing nine tongues. *Oṃ raṃ*, salutation to Agni, who holds a spear in his hand; in the southeast, [he is] mounted on a corpse.

One should always meditate upon Antaka (the God of Death), who holds a staff in his hand, resembles a dark blue cloud, is accompanied by Yami, and is seated upon a buffalo. Oṃ saṃyamāya daṇḍahastāya namaḥ. To the south [is he] accompanied by the Goddess, possessing great power...
At the time of the oblation, one should meditate upon Nirṛti, who has three eyes and holds a sword in his hand;
[the mantra is]:
*Oṃ kṣaṃ namo nirṛtaye khaḍgahastāya*. To the west, situated in the southwest, is Varuṇa together with his goddess.

One should always meditate upon Varuṇa, whose abode is the ocean and who holds a noose in his hand, for the pacification of the multitude of obstacles during the fire sacrifice (*homa*): *Oṃ vaṃ, obeisance to Varuṇa, the holder of the noose in his hand*, in the west.
[And one should meditate upon] Samīraṇa (Vāyu), mounted upon a deer, swift, and holding a banner in his hand.
At the time of the fire-oblation (homa), one should meditate upon the friend of fire (Agni) as endowed with power:
*Oṃ yaṃ*, salutation to Vāyu, who holds a banner in his hand. To the north of Vāyu is Kuvera, the friend of Tryambaka, the bestower of all perfections, the king of the Yakṣas, who holds a mace.

One should meditate upon him for the pacification of obstacles: "Oṃ kuṃ, salutations to Kuvera, who holds a mace; in the north, one should always meditate upon Maheśāna mounted on a bull, pure as clear crystal, with a trident in his hand, together with the Goddess."

One should meditate on the three-eyed Īśāna with the mantra "Oṃ Śūṃ, obeisance to Īśāna, who holds a trident in his hand. In the northeast (Īśāna), one should meditate upon Brahmā, seated upon a lotus, four-faced, holding a lotus and a water-pot (kamaṇḍalu), the treasure-house of the Vedas during the fire sacrifice.
Furthermore, the wise one should meditate upon Viṣṇu above, with the mantra *oṃ āṃ brahmaṇe padmahastāya namaḥ*,
as four-armed and adorned with a conch, discus, mace, and lotus, endowed with Śrī,
and wearing yellow garments; [meditating] on Viṣṇu with the mantra *oṃ hlāṃ viṣṇave*.

*Oṃ* *cakrahastāya namaḥ* (Salutation to the one with the discus in hand), below: *Oṃ jyauṃ agner niṣkrāmaṇaṃ karomi svāhā* (I perform the emergence of Agni, svāhā), (3) *saṃpā* (3). *Oṃ vyauṃ agner ādityadarśanaṃ karomi svāhā* (I perform the manifestation of the Sun for Agni, svāhā), (3) *saṃpā* (3). *Oṃ oṃ oṃ śivāgnaye namaḥ* (Salutation to the auspicious Fire).

Thus the worship: *Oṃ oṃ oṃ, I perform the naming of Agni as Śivāgni, svāhā* (3 times). *Saṃpā* (3 times). *Oṃ, I perform the release of the bracelet of Vāgīśī, svāhā* (3 times). *Saṃpā* (3 times). [The bracelet of] Vāgīśī...

Releasing the form [of the deity], [one says]: "Oṃ, obeisance to Brahmā; Oṃ, svāhā to Brahmā" (three times). "May Brahmā forgive me. One should release the previous seat. On the right: "Oṃ, obeisance to Rudra; Oṃ, svāhā to Rudra" (three times). "May Rudra forgive me."
He should release that southern seat with "Oṃ Viṣṇave namaḥ" and "Oṃ Viṣṇave svāhā. Having asked Viṣṇu's forgiveness, he should release that western seat. In the north, [he should recite] "Oṃ Sa..."
Oṃ, obeisance to Sadāśiva; Oṃ Sadāśivāya Svāhā.
(3) May Sadāśiva forgive me. One should release the northern seat.
Oṃ Juṃ, obeisance to Vāgīśvarī; Oṃ Juṃ Vāgīśvaryai Svāhā. (10)

O Vāgīśvarī, may you forgive [this]; O Goddess who bestows liberation through the senses of creation, maintenance, and dissolution—homage to you, O Vāgīśvarī! Depart, O Goddess, to your own abode. Then Vāgīśvarī should release the seat.
The fuel and oblation are one cubit in length. *Oṃ oṃ oṃ, I satiate the Śiva-fire, svāhā* (25).
Now, the consecration of the sacrificial ladle (*sruc*): *Oṃ phaṭ, I perform the sprinkling, phaṭ*.
Likewise, the veiling with the water of Śiva.
First, heating [the vessel] for a moment; then rotating it; then sprinkling with water using the tip of a *darbha* blade;
then touching it with that same tip; then sprinkling again, rotating, heating, and touching it with the middle part; then rotating and heating once more, and sprinkling.

With the root-mantra, touch its base; then, having placed it face down upon the back of a *darbha* blade, perform the anointing with Śiva and Śakti: "Gandhaṃ namaḥ" (Scent, obeisance), "Arghyaṃ namaḥ" (Water-offering, obeisance), "Puṣpaṃ namaḥ" (Flower, obeisance). [Then] face upward.
Having performed "Obeisance to Śiva" and "Obeisance to Śakti," then follows the consecration of the clarified butter (*ājya*).

This consists of: placing the clarified butter on the fire, pouring it out, placing it in a vessel that has been thoroughly sprinkled with water, and heating it in the pot; thus he describes the twelve consecrations.
Oṃ haḥ phaṭ! I perform the sprinkling with the auspicious water, phaṭ.
Oṃ haiṃ! I veil [it] with huṃ; thus, the veiling is performed with the *liṅgamudrā*.
Oṃ haḥ phaṭ! I warm [it] in the fire of Śiva, namaḥ.

*Oṃ hai*, [I perform] the heating; *huṃ*, [I perform] the dismissal in the south-eastern direction for the purpose of clear manifestation of light through the upward holding. *Oṃ haḥ phaṭ*, [I] cause [the fire] to whirl *phaṭ*, [reciting] this mantra with the *astra* around the perimeter of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*).

Having taken two *darbha* blades, each a span (*prādeśa*) long and shaped like a serpent’s noose (*nāgapāśa*), with the thumbs of both hands for the purpose of rotating [the vessel] and establishing the womb-vessel (*yoni*),
one should lead the clarified butter (*ājya*) three times toward the east and then away from it.
One should perform the immersion (*samplavana*) and the leaping-up (*utplavana*): three times facing east with "Oṃ haḥ phaṭ, I perform the immersion, phaṭ";
and three times facing west with "Oṃ haḥ phaṭ, the leaping-up."
Saying "karomi phaṭ," one should perform the removal of the insubstantial parts;

having kindled a torch of *darbha* grass, one gazes at the vessel of clarified butter with "Oṃ jyauṃ prekṣaṇaṃ karomi namaḥ. There, by the gazing upon that splendor, [one overcomes] the splendor of others.
One should prepare the clarified butter (*ājya*); this is the consecration (*saṃskāra*) known as illumination.
With that very *darbha*-wick torch, one should rotate [the vessel] three times in every direction; this is the *nīrājana*. "Oṃ hūṃ, I perform the encircling with fire (*paryagnīkaraṇa*); obeisance."
Thus, one should cast [the oblation] into the fire with *oṃ haḥ phaṭ*. The gazing [at the fire] is performed with the water of Śiva (*śivāmbhas*).

The consecration as nectar (*amṛtīkaraṇa*) is performed with the root mantra and its limbs. One should worship with the root mantra; this is the consecration of the clarified butter (*ājya-saṃskāra*). With the face of Sadyojāta, [one recites] *laṃ*; with Aghora... [and so on].

*Raṃ*, with the face of Aghora, I unite with the face of Tatpuruṣa, svāhā! (3) *Yaṃ*, with the face of Tatpuruṣa, I unite with the face of Īśāna, svāhā! (3) *Kṣaṃ*, with the face of Īśāna, I unite [with the center], svāhā! (3)

"Oṃ hūṃ, I perform the visualization of the three channels; namaḥ. With this, one should place two *darbha* blades, with their tips pointing east, in the *ājya* vessel with their tips pointing east. In the center [of the vessel], one should offer:
"Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the power of will (*icchā-śakti*); Oṃ, to the abode of fire, Suṣumṇā..."
*Oṃ namaḥ* to the left of oneself; *oṃ hrīṃ kriyāśaktaye namaḥ*.
*Oṃ saḥ somadhāmne iḍāyai namaḥ* to the right of oneself; *oṃ hūṃ jñānaśaktaye namaḥ*. *Oṃ juṃ sūryadhāmne piṅgalāyai namaḥ*. Now, [the worship] of Agni.

Reciting "Oṃ, I perform the conceptualization of the three parts of the auspicious fire; Namaḥ," one should offer two fuel-sticks (samidh), each a span (prādeśa) in length, with their tips facing upward. Then, reciting "Oṃ Oṃ, obeisance to Sūrya who resides in the Piṅgalā [nāḍī]," one should place them to the left of the fire.
The worship of the [three] castings: in the center, *oṃ juṃ suṣumṇā-āśrayāya agnaye namaḥ*;
on one's own right, *oṃ saḥ iḍā-āśrayāya somāya namaḥ*;
and on the left, *oṃ juṃ saḥ agnaye svāhā*. Thus [it is said].

From the southern portion of the *jyā*, in the southern portion of the fire, [he offers] clarified butter with the mantra "Oṃ *mūla* to Soma, svāhā"; from the northern portion of the *jyā*, outside the northern portion, [he offers] clarified butter with "Oṃ *juṃ saḥ* to Agni and Soma, svāhā"; and from the middle portion of the clarified butter, outside...

In the middle portion, during the bright fortnight, [one offers] with "Oṃ juṃ saḥ agnaye svāhā" the clarified butter from the right side outside the right side [of the fire]; and with "Oṃ juṃ saḥ sūryāya svāhā" the clarified butter from the left side outside the left side [of the fire].

Oṃ juṃ saḥ, svāhā to Agni and Sūrya—thus [one offers] from the middle portion of the clarified butter (*ājya*) into the middle portion of the fire; this is for the dark fortnight (*kṛṣṇapakṣa*). Oṃ juṃ saḥ, svāhā, I perform the consumption of Śivāgni—(3) *samyā* (3)—now the clarified butter (*ājya*).
Vision is declared to be the essence of clarified butter (*ājya*); clarified butter is the supreme remover of sin.
Clarified butter is the food of the gods, and in clarified butter the worlds are established.
Whatever impurity I have incurred through [actions] pertaining to the heavens, the atmosphere, or the earth—[may it be removed by this].

May all that [impurity] go to destruction through contact with this clarified butter (ājya). For the purpose of warding off the sins acquired by my own speech, mind, and body, and for the gratification of my chosen deity, I offer this to the auspicious fire (Śivāgni).
"I offer the bow; obeisance. Thus is the inspection of the clarified butter (ājya).
[He beholds] Agni, the god who kindles the flame, adorning himself manifoldly with flames that embellish the sky, holding a rosary and a water-pot (kamaṇḍalu).
The god is red in color like fire, with three eyes, holding a tooth and the gesture of fearlessness in his hands;
he is mounted upon a parrot, possesses four arms with a spear in one hand,
is draped in a deer skin, and bestows boons upon the sacrificer.

At the time of the fire-oblation (homa), one should contemplate [the deity] as five-faced. [Recite]: "Oṃ juṃ saḥ! O Śivāgni, may all the purificatory rites (saṃskāras) beginning with the birth-ceremony (cūḍā) and continuing through childhood and so forth, up to the first solid food (prāśana), be fully accomplished—vauṣaṭ! Thus [one should offer].
Then, having offered [oblations] with one’s own name and syllables, one should worship Viṣṇu in the cup. There, one should prepare a sacred thread (*pavitra*) joined with flowers, seeds, and sesame,
accompanied by the recitation of one’s own name and ending with "namas" and the [mantra] beginning with "śaṅkha-cakra-ga."

One should meditate upon the Lord Viṣṇu, who is adorned with lotuses, possesses four arms, has the Śrīvatsa mark and the Kaustubha gem upon his chest, and is decorated with a forest garland; one should meditate on the Lord in this manner as the immutable. Oṃ, let us know the seat of Viṣṇu... vi...
We meditate upon that Supreme Viṣṇu; may that Viṣṇu inspire us.
(3) Oṃ bhūḥ, I invoke the Puruṣa, obeisance. Oṃ hūṃ bhuvaḥ, I invoke the Puruṣa, obeisance. Oṃ hrīṃ svaḥ, I invoke the Puruṣa.
*Oṃ namo oṃ hrīṃ huṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ puruṣam āvāhayāmi namo oṃ bhagavan viṣṇo āgaccha (2) oṃ bhagavan viṣṇo svāgatam tiṣṭha (2) saṃnidhatsva (2) haṃ haṃ haṃ bhaga.*

Oṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ Viṣṇo, accept the water for the feet; namaḥ. Oṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ Viṣṇo, accept the arghya; svāhā. Likewise, accept the anointing; likewise, the unbroken rice and flowers; vauṣaṭ. Thus, accept the worship with the five offerings; vauṣaṭ.
Six times: *Oṃ huṃ viṣṇave namaḥ*. Then he should cause [the sacrificer] to receive the command: "Oṃ!
Sacrifices have been commenced by practitioners either for the sake of cattle or for their own sake;
O Blessed One, by your grace, may our sacrifices be free from defects."
Thus concludes the worship of the *camasa* vessel. Now follows the consecration of the *caru*.

Having drawn a mandala to the left of oneself according to the rule for the fire-ritual (*agnidakṣa*), and having spread *darbha* grass with its tips pointing eastward, one should perform the placement of the seat with the mantra "To the Support-Power (*ādhāraśakti*), obeisance" (*namas*).

Having worshipped [the deity] and placed the *caru* offering upon that, having worshipped the *caru* with the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*) and the limb mantras (*aṅga-mantras*), having rendered it nectarine (*amṛtīkṛta*) by means of the Amṛteśa mudrā, and having ignited a blade of *darbha* grass with "phaṭ," he says: "I perform the lustration (*nīrājana*); phaṭ."
Having rotated it three times over the glowing embers and cast it into the fire, one should sprinkle it with auspicious water (*śivāmbhas*).
Then, with the *astra-mantra*, one should place the stirring-ladle (*mekṣaṇa*) together with its base in front [of the fire].
Reciting "Oṃ juṃ saḥ, become well-heated, svāhā," one should offer it into the fire.
With "Iti carau evaṃ juṃ su-tapta-bhava svāhā," [he offers] into the fire;
with "Iti carau evaṃ vyoḥ huṃ jyok phaṭ," having placed it upon the fire, he then [places] on the ground to his right [the seat] with "Āsanāya namaḥ."
Having spread out darbha grass, one should take down the sacrificial porridge (caru).

For the cooling of the affliction caused by the moon's influence and for the pacification of the fault of exhaustion, one should perform the rite with the root mantra together with its six ancillaries and the *vauṣaṭ* exclamation:
*Oṃ oṃ oṃ suśīto bhava vauṣaṭ svāhā*. Thus ends the ritual procedure.
In the fire: *Oṃ juṃ suśīto bhava svāhā*. In the charu: *Hā*. In the fire: *Evaṃ vyoḥ hūṃ jyot phaṭ*. Again, with the Soma-mantra:
*Namaḥ pūjanam oṃ syuṃ jagadāpyāyanakatre somāya*.
Saying "Ya-namaḥ," and saying "Oṃ phaṭ, I cover the caru, namaḥ," one should cover it with *darbha* grass;
then, saying "Oṃ huṃ, I protect the caru, namaḥ," one should place flowers on top. Then, upon the *jālā-liṅga*, [place] a new lotus.
One should fashion and worship them as follows: Oṃ, obeisance to Prabhā;
Oṃ, obeisance to Dīpti; Oṃ, obeisance to Prakāśā; [obeisance] to Arcā, Marīci, Sthāpinī, Ruci, Karālī, and Lelihānā.
One should contemplate and worship [the tongues] in the form of flames upon the *jvālā-liṅga*.

Now, the worship of the nine tongues within the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) is as follows: *Oṃ*, salutation to the Giver of Sovereignty (*rājyārthadā*) in the East; *Oṃ*, salutation to the Mother of Burning (*dāhajanani*) in the Southeast (*āgneya*).

Oṃ, salutation to the Bestower of Death in the south; Oṃ, salutation to the Destroyer of Enemies in the southwest; Oṃ, salutation to the Enchanter in the west; Oṃ, salutation to the Exorciser in the northwest;
Oṃ, salutation to the Bestower of Wealth in the north; Oṃ, salutation to Liberation...
"Oṃ *dāyāyai* namaḥ to the Īśāna [corner]; Oṃ *sarvasiddhipradāyai* namaḥ in the center.
Having thus worshipped, the homa ends with *svāhā*. Then the full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) with the mantra: 'Oṃ juṃ saḥ, I fashion the tongues in the Śiva-fire, svāhā.'"

HĀV AUṢAṬ! OṂ! May there be the presence of the tongues of the fire of Śiva; SVĀHĀ VAUṢAṬ! One should meditate upon the Fire-god as having red matted locks, wearing red garments, with his left side occupied by Svāhā, possessing two arms, and having red eyes—O Parrot!
One should contemplate the god Agni, who is seated upon a chariot, adorned with a flaming beard,
as the purifier of the offerings to gods and ancestors. Homage to Agni, who is mounted upon a parrot, accompanied by Svāhā, and holding a spear in his hand.
Thus is the worship.

Thereafter, having taken the tip of the flame of the fire and having meditated upon the consciousness of the fire (vahni-caitanya), one should say: "Oṃ juṃ, O Śivāgni, I grasp the tip of your flame, namas," while the index finger is bent into a hook-shape.

Having taken it in through the right nostril according to the *sadgṛhya* [method], and having united it with the fire of consciousness residing in the heart, one should proceed through the heart, throat, palate,
and the space between the eyebrows in sequence to the *brahmarandhra*; there, she who possesses two breasts [resides].
Having milked the wish-fulfilling cow (Manogadhenu), one should churn her milk; imagining that the sacrificial oblation (havir) has emerged as clarified butter (ghṛta), one should take that ghee and,
by that same sequence, descend today with the root mantra.

Having performed the *aśakti-homa* according to one's capacity, the final oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) should be offered as follows: Oṃ! Into the fire of my own self, which blazes with the oblation of dharma and adharma, I perpetually offer the movement of the *suṣumṇā* through the mind, with the ladle of the senses, while remaining established in the flow of the imperishable.

*Myahaṃ svāhā*. Then, having united the external fire with the fire of consciousness (*caitanya-vahni*), one should meditate upon the form of Amṛteśvara within the middle tongue of that fire through the state of Śiva-nature, just as one would meditate upon the Lord of Gods within one's own self.

The all-pervading Lord, whose radiance is equal to ten million moons, who resembles jasmine, the moon, cow’s milk, and the Himalayan mountain; who is adorned with ornaments such as white pearls, moonstones, and crystals; and whose limbs are smeared with white sandalwood and camphor.
[He is] grey with the dust of the Rakshasas, overflowing with the vast waves of the shimmering nectar of the moon,
situated in the center of the lunar disc, having one face and three eyes, seated upon a white lotus, and [with arms] bound...

One should visualize [the deity] seated upon a lotus throne, four-armed and large-eyed, with his right hand displaying the gesture of granting boons; he is as full as the moon and is worshipped with entirely white offerings, held in the left hand.

One should remember the *manusmṛti-dhyāna*; having remembered it, one should place flowers in the joined palms (*añjali*) and perform the invocation (*āvāhana*) of the deity with: *Oṃ bhagavan āgaccha namaḥ*—this is the invocation. *Bhagavan tiṣṭha svāhā*—this is the [staying].
O Blessed One, be present! O Blessed One, become completely absorbed! Bha-vuṃ phaṭ! O Blessed One, be present! O Blessed One, enter into this! Oṃ huṃ! O Blessed One, I perform the veiling, namaḥ.

Having thus veiled [the deity] with "O Blessed One, I make [you] immortal, *namaḥ*," and having rendered [him] immortal, then from the *argha* vessel [one offers]: "O Blessed One, accept the water for washing the feet, *namaḥ*; O Blessed One, accept the water for sipping, *svadhā*."

Thus, accept this worship with the five offerings (*pañcopacāra-pūjā*), *vauṣaṭ*. Then, one should worship the Root [Mantra] together with its limbs and the Goddess. Having performed the worship of the door, the worship of the Guru, and the section concerning the seat beginning with Ādhāraśakti, [one worships] Aghora.
The face with its limbs, Aghoreśvarī with her limbs and faces, the Niṣkala (partless) form with its limbs,
the Bhairava-enclosure, the Weapon-enclosure, the seven enclosures beginning with the Vidyeśas,
the eight Mothers beginning with Brāhmī, and the eight names beginning with Bhava.
Having fully worshipped the enclosure of Heruka and the others, Vaṭuka and the others, the Kṣetrapālas, and the six mantras beginning with *Oṃ*,
one should then cook the sacrificial pap (*caru*) previously prepared in a vessel with the six flavors, using the root mantra together with its limbs (*aṅga*).

Having performed the worship, [he offers] into the fire with the mantra "oṃ juṃ saḥ saṃpātaṃ karomi svāhā," [and then] two oblations of rice and ghee; thus, with oblations of all the materials suitable for the *homa*, such as fuel-sticks, barley, sesame seeds, and so forth.
One should perform the *saṃpāta* rite with three [offerings]; then, [the offering] for the *kṣetrapālas* is in the *kalaśa*,
while that for the *lokapālas* is in the fire, near the sacrificial fire.
Taking some food— such as fish, meat, or cakes—
and having offered it as a *naivedya* before the striking of the hour, [one recites]: *oṃ bhairavavaktraṃ śivāgnivaktreṣvanusandadhe svāhā* (3).

With clarified butter: *Oṃ bhairavaktrajihvāḥ śivāgnivaktrajihvāsv anusandadhe svāhā*. Then, having uttered the root mantra (*mūlamantra*), [one should offer it] from the heart through the nostril into the fire.
Having emerged, one should enter by the south of Aṣṭhaṇḍileśa;
likewise, having entered through the enclosure, one should enter by the south of the fire. This is the junction of the channels (*nāḍī-sandhāna*); thus [ends] the section on fire.
The ritual means (*sādhana*) is for the purpose of turning [the deity] toward bestowing grace.
A fire-oblation (*samiddhoma*) should be performed with: *oṃ amṛteśvarabhairavaṃ tarpayāmi svāhā*—(108), (54), (17), (14), (7).

The Lord of Aṅgada [is worshipped] as half of Bhairava with the Goddess, or like Bhairava; likewise for all [the deities] beginning with Gaṇeśa. Then follows the *homa* of the seven enclosures (*saptāvaraṇa*).
Therein, first are the Lords of Knowledge (*vidyeśvaras*): Oṃ hrīṃ, svāhā to Ananta.
Hā oṃ glūṃ to Sūkṣma; oṃ ra ha ru to Śivottama;
oṃ huṃ to Ekanetra; oṃ kṣuṃ to Ekarudra; nluṃ to Trimūrti; oṃ har thaṃ to Śrīkaṇṭha; oṃ śrīṃ to Śaṅkhaṇḍin; [and now] Athaga.
Ṇeśāḥ Oṃ Rāṃ Rīṃ Rūṃ to Nandin; Oṃ Māṃ Mīṃ Slkuṃ to Mahākāla; Oṃ Stāṃ Bhṛṃ to Bhṛṅgirudra; Oṃ Gatkuṃ Gaṃ to Gaṇapati; Oṃ Vrāṃ to Vṛṣabha; Hsāṃ Kuṃ to Kumāra; Oṃ Hrīṃ Saḥ.
[Offerings] for Ambikā and for Caṇḍeśvara; then the world-protectors:
*laṃ* to Indra, who holds the thunderbolt in his hand; *rūṃ* to Agni, who holds the spear in his hand; *maṃ* to Yama, who holds the staff in his hand; *kṣaṃ* to Nirṛti, who holds the sword...

Vaṃ to the hand-bearing Varuṇa who holds a noose in his hand; yaṃ to Vāyu who holds a banner in his hand; kuṃ to Kuvera who holds a mace in his hand; śū to Īśāna who holds a trident in his hand; āṃ to Brahmā [who holds] a lotus.
To the hand, *hlāṃ* to Viṣṇu who holds the discus in his hand; *atha mā taraḥ*.
*Oṃ jamaraya rthaṃ jayāyai svāhā*. *Oṃ rasarthaṃ vijayāyai*. *Yaṃ subhagāyai*. *Raṃ durbha*.
Gāyai, Jamara-rtha-jayantyai, Paṃrtha-hinyai, Oṃhasa-rathaṃ, Aparājitāyai, Jaṃkarālyai.
Now the enclosure of the planets (grahāvaraṇa): Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ.
To Sūrya.

Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ, for the Sun; saha rthaṃ, for the Moon; ra ha ra rthaṃ, for Mars; ha sa rthaṃ, for Mercury; ra sa rthaṃ, for Jupiter; hrīṃ, for Venus; kṣa ma ra rthaṃ, for Saturn; ṭūṃ, for Rāhu; hrīṃ.
For the sake of the Ketu [planet], the protection against the nāgas: Oṃ, to Ananta-nāgarāja,
Vāsuki, Padma, Mahāpadma, Takṣaka,
Kārkoṭaka, Kulika, and Vajra— phaṭ!
To Śakti, to Daṇḍa, to Khaḍga, to Pāśa, Phaṭ! To Dhvaja, to Gadā, to Triśūla, to Padma, to Hala; Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Vrauṃ, to Māheśvarī, to Kaumārī, to Vaiṣṇavī, to Vārāhī, to Aindrī.

To Cāmuṇḍā, to Mahālakṣmī; then the enclosure of the Lords of the Field (Kṣetrapālas); to Heruka and others, to Vaṭuka and others. Then, with clarified butter: Oṃ juṃ saḥ, I satiate Amṛteśvara Bhairava, svāhā. (24)
Or (14), or (7) for each of the limbs, then (1): thereafter, the full [offering]:
*oṃ juṃ saḥ sarvamantracakratṛptir astu vauṣaṭ*. Now the second: *oṃ juṃ saḥ bhairavāpyāyanam astu vauṣaṭ*. *a*...

The third [mantra] is: *Oṃ juṃ saḥ nyūnātiriktaṃ pūrayāmi vauṣaṭ*. By this offering of fuel-sticks (*samid-dhoma*), may all the deities be satisfied and grant boons. Now follows the food-offering (*anna-homa*) by means of dividing it into three parts.
The *syahoma* (libation): Oṃ Gaṃ, I satiate Vināyaka, svāhā!
(10) Oṃ Hāṃ, I satiate Bhūtadhātrī, svāhā! (10) Oṃ Śrīṃ, [I satiate] Śrī, svāhā! (10) Oṃ Juṃ, I satiate the day of consecration (*adhivāsadinam*), svāhā! (10)

Oṃ juṃ, may there be success in the consecration; svāhā! (10) Oṃ huṃ, I purify through atonement; svāhā! (10) Oṃ huṃ, may there be purity through atonement; svāhā! (10) Oṃ hūṃ, I fulfill what is deficient and remove what is excessive.
Svāhā (10). Oṃ juṃ saḥ, I satiate Amṛtabhairava with Svāhā (108), or (54). Oṃ juṃ saḥ, I satiate Amṛtalakṣmī with Svāhā (10). Then, as for the mantras of Gaṇeśa and the others:
One should perform the satiation according to the extent of one's capacity, as well as the oblation for the seven enclosures (*saptāvaraṇahoma*).

Then, [the deities are]: the Full Oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*), the Lords of the Gates, the Nine Cavities, the Heart, Vāstu, Gaṇeśa, the Mind, and the objects of the senses beginning with sound, as well as the Gurus.
The ten vital breaths (samīra) consist of the foundational power (ādhāra-śakti),

while the Lord of Consciousness (cit-deva), accompanied by the power of reflective awareness (vimarśa-śakti), possesses the six qualities (ṣāḍguṇya) as His limbs; the world-protectors (lokeśas) are His instruments, and such is His majesty.
We praise that Lord of the Eye: *oṃ juṃ saḥ sarvamantracakratṛptir astu vauṣaṭ* (5).
*Devam svadhā*—*oṃ juṃ saḥ bhairavāpyāyanam astu vauṣaṭ*.
[To] the Supreme Haṃsa situated in the central breath...

The vital breaths (prāṇas), numbering three and a half crores, which reside in the hair-pores of the body and possess forms characterized by subtle discernment— He who reverses them into the nature of mantra is the supreme Svacchandanaṭha.
Obeisance to the supreme, eternal splendor of the form of Bhairava, who bestows all prosperity;
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, may there be the fulfillment of any deficiency or excess in the ritual procedure, svāhā!
Then follows the libation (*tarpaṇa*): by means of this internal oblation (*antahoma*), may Śiva [be satisfied].
May the River, together with her limbs and her goddesses, be pleased; may she be pleased.
Now, the mantra for the animal sacrifice: having well-bathed the animal, which is complete in all auspicious characteristics, [with the mantra]:
"O Vārāhī, Yamunā, Gaṅgā, Karatoyā, Sarasvatī..."
May the river Vairī, Candrabhāgā, Sindhu, and the formidable ocean come to the place of the sacrificial animals;
and whatever others there are known by those names, may they come. I offer svadhā to your speech, I offer svadhā to your nose, I offer svadhā to your navel.
I consecrate your eye with svadhā; I consecrate your ear with svadhā;
may your speech swell; may your nose swell; may your ear swell; may your eye swell; may your navel swell; [may] the animal [swell], O animal-guardian.

"To Him who dwells on the Golden Peak (Hemakūṭa) of the Nāśāya mountain, the Supreme-Non-Supreme, the Ultimate Cause, whose form is ageless— Padme Padme Mahāpadme Padmāvati Māye Svāhā! Thus is the inspection from the vessel of the fivefold offering (pañcārghya).
One should sprinkle [the victim] with the root mantra: *pheṃ pheṃ paśūhana huṃ phaṭ*.
Having sprinkled [him], one should then take the cord and bind the victim at the head with:
*oṃ hrīṃ phaṭ paśuṃ bandhaya bandhaya*. Then, one should station [the victim] before the Goddess.

Having sprinkled [the guest] with water from the *argha* vessel using the root mantra (*mūla*), having veiled him with the *kavaca* mantra, and having rendered him nectar-like by means of the *dhenu-mudrā*, one should offer the *pādya* and other services while reciting the mantra: "O you who possess the form of the supreme *paśu*. Then again—
One should worship with flowers: "Oṃ, obeisance to Rudhiravadanā" on the head;
"obeisance to Caṇḍikā" on the cheek; "obeisance to Sarasvatī" on the mouth;
"obeisance to Śraddhā" and "obeisance to Medhā" on the two eyes; [and] to Bṛhaspati...
*Yenamaḥ prāṇadāyai namaḥ caṃdrādityābhyāṃ namaḥ* at the two nostrils; *loṃ hrīṃ bahurūpāyai namaḥ pracaṇḍarūpāyai namaḥ ugranāsāyai namaḥ* at the two ears; *vaiṣṇavyai namaḥ*.
Salutation to Padmanābhī on the tongue; salutation to Viṣṇu on the belly; salutation to Śrī on the navel; salutation to Rudhirotamā and Bhairavī on the private parts;
[on] the feet: "Enjoin this sacrificial animal to heaven; manifest liberation."
Oṃ hrīṃ! To the destroyer of obstacles presiding over the lunar disc, I dedicate this sacrificial animal for my own purpose; svāhā! In the ritual procedure for Caṇḍī: Oṃ hili hili!
To the one who assumes many forms, to the fierce Durgā, [I dedicate] this sacrificial animal.
Engage me in my own welfare; manifest liberation! Oṃ hrīṃ! To the destroyer of obstacles presiding over the lunar disc, I offer this victim—svāhā!
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ! To the one who embodies all deities, in the form of an offering...
I offer this scent to Yāmuka-paśu; *namaḥ*. To the unbroken flowers, *vauṣaṭ*.

One should recite the Paśu-gāyatrī three times into the right ear of the animal: "We know the one who is the bond of the animal (*paśupāśāya*); for the one who is the womb of the universe (*viśvagarbhāya*)."

Dhīmahi tat no jīvaḥ pracodayāt (3). Oṃ hrīṃ huṃ phaṭ, may you go to the form of Śiva, svāhā. Oṃ juṃ saḥ ha sa kṣa ma la va ra ya rthaṃ, may you go to the form of Śiva, svāhā (7). [Recite] at the root of the ear.

O fair-faced one, this great mantra of the Goddess is difficult to obtain even for the gods; he who recites it seven times at the root of the ear attains that which grants liberation, and as a bound soul (paśu), he shall realize the principle of Śiva. Whoever [recites] this...

The hell-being who was a butcher of animals [is released] from the Vainaja [hell]. Then, taking scents and water for sprinkling, and reciting the root mantra: "From this day forward, may [the name], of such-and-such lineage, be long-lived; may there be no famine..."

The fruit equal to the horse sacrifice (*aśvamedha*), which culminates in the cessation of suffering and the state of supreme bliss; the ascent upon a magnificent celestial chariot (*vimāna*) adorned with rows of banners; the departure to the world of the former goddesses; and the attainment of eternal meditative absorption (*samādhi*).
Having said, "Desiring unbroken victory, I offer this sacrificial animal (paśu) to you, O glorious [Name] deity; salutations!
Be gracious," one should place flowers, unhusked rice (akṣata), water, and so forth upon the head of the animal.
Then, having offered the nectar-like food-oblation (*naivedya*), and then holding the head of the sacrificial animal, one should recite this mantra: "Animals were created for the sake of sacrifice;
the slaughter of the animal is for the sake of sacrifice; therefore, I shall cause you to be slain."

O Yajñovodha, this body (piṇḍa) is dependent upon Śiva; you have attained the state of Śiva through me. Arise, O beast (paśu), for you were not Śiva [before]. Become Śiva! You were created as a beast by the gods for the sake of sacrifice.

O sinless one, you must now be sacrificed by me with great enthusiasm; for in the past, you were fashioned as a sacrificial animal, and through the offering of your own flesh as a tribute, I shall perform my desired worship.
"Give me back this animal which was given by me; you must always perform its use within the sacrifice,
for [the gods] are satisfied by the offering of meat and blood."
Salutations to you who take the form of an animal for the sake of destroying the misfortunes of the donor;
for the benefit of the worlds, an animal has now been created by me.
Sprinkled with water for the pleasure of the deities, deliver yourself and me from this state.
"Having bound him in fetters for the sake of protection, you have been appointed by me for his liberation.
Having generated delight in the Goddess, go to heaven, O best of men. Having thus awakened the sacrificial animal (*paśu*), one should worship the sword with the root-mantra (*mūlavidyā*).
Having drawn forth the sword and placed it before him, one should sprinkle it with scented water, unbroken rice, and water while reciting: *hrīṃ kili (2) vajreśvari lohadaṇḍāyai namaḥ*.
Then, having worshipped it again with scented water, unbroken rice, and water, [one should perform] at the beginning...

At the place of the fist, one should worship with "Oṃ, obeisance to Vāgīśvarī and Brahmā"; in the middle, with "obeisance to Sāvitrī and Viṣṇu"; and at the tip, with "obeisance to Umā and Maheśvara. Having worshipped thus and held it, one should consecrate it with the mantra: *kha*.

"O Lord of the Sword, you who are intent on the destruction of the demons and the accomplishment of the gods' work, may the animal sacrifice be swiftly [accomplished] by you; salutations to you! Having consecrated the sword with this mantra, one should worship it once again with the *khaḍgī* [mantra].

Salutations to the seed-syllable of the sword; salutations to the self whose essence is the *hrīṃ* seed-syllable, served by the vowels encircled by the serpent-girdle. You are the sword that shattered the lords of the Daityas, with a sharp edge and difficult to approach, the womb of prosperity.
"Victory to you, and salutations to you, the protector of Dharma! Having thus spoken, he took up that sword [reciting]: "Oṃ hrīṃ klīṃ, salutations to Caṇḍikā, the iron staff!
Oṃ hrīṃ klīṃ, may this sacrificial animal [be for] satisfaction..."

With the mantra "Kuru (2) Muru (2) He Amukadevi Gṛhāṇa Svāhā," one should cut [the effigy] with a rhinoceros-horn blade. Then, having oneself become the form of the Goddess and remaining free from conceptual construction, one should strike it with a single blow.
The practitioner, free from conceptual thought, should have another person cut [the limb] with their hand; having taken that blood and brought it,
he should draw a maṇḍala consisting of a circle, a triangle, a crescent, and a square on his own left side.
Having sprinkled [the area] with the Astra-mantra and worshipped the foundational powers (ādhāraśakti),
one should place a vessel of blood upon it; this skull is the abode for the slaughter of the Siddhas residing within the essence of the blood-fluid.

Reciting "gṛhṇa svāhā," one should cast [the offering] among the guardians of the field (*kṣetrapāla*). Having brought the head and the flesh together and placed them before the Goddess, one should offer the food-oblation (*naivedya*) with the root mantra. This is the procedure for the offering of the sacrificial fee (*balidāna-vidhi*). Now follows the oblation of clarified butter (*ājyahoma*).

Oṃ *vibhraddakṣiṇahasta* etc.; this is the meditation (*dhyāna*). Of this Śrī Gaṇapatimantra, Brahmā is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the meter (*chandas*), and the illustrious Mahāgaṇapati is the deity (*devatā*). Gaṃ vī hrīṃ śa kuru (2).

The application (*viniyoga*) for the *homa* [is as follows]: [one should perform] the invocation of Agni with flowers and so forth, according to the prescribed rules, using the *argha* vessel and other implements; [the mantra is]:
"To Gaṇeśa, the one with the curved trunk, I offer obeisance; may He grant me success. [This is recited] for the purpose of removing obstacles.
Oṃ, salutation to Gaṇapati, svāhā! (10) Oṃ, I worship here the Lord of the Gaṇas, who has two arms, a face like a lotus, who wears deep red garments, who is auspicious,
and who bestows both fearlessness and boons.
Oṃ gūṃ saḥ, svāhā to Gaṇapativallabhā.
Ā ardhaṃ gāṃ, namaḥ svāhā to the heart. Gāṃ, svāhā to the head.
Gūṃ, vaṣaṭ svāhā to the tuft of hair. Ga, svāhā to the armor.
*Gauṃ* to the eyes, *vauṣaṭ svāhā*; *gaḥ* to the weapon, *phaṭ svāhā*.

Then follows the ten-fold portion for the limbs (*aṅgānām daśāṃśaḥ*), and then the full oblation (*pūrṇā*). [One should meditate upon] the elephant-faced one, inconceivable, with sharp tusks, three eyes, a large belly, and infinite teeth.
I worship Śrī Gaṇeśa, who holds a rosary, an axe, and a pair of lotus-cups in his hands, and who is seated upon a pair of lions;
then follows the libation with "Mūla-ante vauṣaṭ" at the secret place, and "tataḥ pūrṇā".

The offering for cessation: Oṃ! [I worship him] whose face blazes like ten million fires at the end of an aeon, who is the color of vermilion powder and the *japā* flower, wearing a red crown, possessing two eyes, seated upon the center of a white lotus, and adorned with various ornaments.
I worship Him whose face is smiling, who wears red garments, who is composed of consciousness, who is like the sun, and who holds a golden lotus and a jewel-pitcher in His two arms.
Having offered a flower into the fire, [one recites] this [mantra]: "The venerable Brahmā is the seer, the Ṛg-veda is the meter, and Savitṛ..."

*Tāde* hrīṃ vī saḥ śa oṃ; having performed the invocation (*āvāhana*) and other rites in the fire sacrifice (*homa*), [one should offer] the water for the feet (*pādya*) and so forth from the *argha* vessel. *Oṃ sūryarūpāya vi sūryajñānāya dhī tannaḥ sūryaḥ* (3 times); *oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ sū*.
Ryāyanamaḥ svāhā. Ā aṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ svāhā.
Arkāya śirase svāhā. Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ jvālinyai śikhāyai vaṣaṭ svāhā. Hrāṃ kavacāya huṃ svāhā. Bhāṃ.

*Netrebhyo vauṣaṭ svāhā; *raḥ astrāya phaṭ svāhā.* I meditate upon the Goddess who has three eyes and two arms, whose hands shine with the gestures of granting boons (*vara*) and fearlessness (*abhaya*), who is seated upon a lotus, whose face is radiant, and who blazes upon the orb of the sun. *Oṃ rāṃ vi...*

Sphurāya-enamaḥ-svāhā (10). May the Sun-god protect us—he who is seated in the full lotus posture, compassionate toward those who have sought refuge, possessing seven horses, holding a lotus in his hand, and having two arms. *Mūlānte vaṣaṭ*.

May the King of the beautiful-crested ones (Śiva), who holds the bell, the golden-made and lovely banner, and the trident, and who performs the secret supreme libation— the offering of cessation— be ever present before the faces of those who worship him.
Remaining thus with such splendor, the youth Kumāra, though of childlike age, offered a flower into the fire. Having offered [the oblation] to this Śrī Kumāra,
[the ritual proceeds with] the invocation (*āvāhana*), the water for the feet (*pādya*), and so forth, accompanied by the *Ṛg* verses of Brahmā and the *Sāman* chants of Kumāra during the *Homa*.
To Kārttikeya, the commander of the army; may Kumāra grant that to us:

*oṃ kluṃ kuṃ kumārāya namaḥ svāhā*. With *kāṃ kīm*, and so forth, there is the six-limbed fire-offering (*ṣaḍaṅgahoma*). Then, [the offering of] the full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*): Himādri, white, two-armed...

One should not forget Kumāra, the first son dear to the daughter of the mountain king, who is seated upon the back of a peacock and surrounded by serpents, the bestower of desired boons; [the mantra is:
*mūlānte vaṣaṭ*, and the libation (*tarpaṇa*) and the offering of water for the restraint (*nirodhārgha*) are likewise performed.
Take refuge in the Lord Amṛteśvara, the primordial deity, who is exceedingly beautiful with a crown of half-moons,
whose face is like the full moon, who is seated upon a lotus throne, who holds a vessel of nectar, a jar, a lotus,
and the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, and who possesses three eyes.

The fire-flower of this [is] the glorious Amṛteśvarabhairava; the lineage of the left-hand deity (Vāmamārga) is Amṛteśvarabhairava; Oṃ Juṃ Saḥ. For the invocation, the water for the feet, and so forth during the homa, [the mantra is]: Oṃ Juṃ Saḥ. Kī. Śa. Oṃ. Kī. Homa-vi. Āvāhana-pādya-ādi. Oṃ Juṃ Saḥ.

Salutation to Amṛteśvarabhairava (108 times). Oṃ juṃ hṛdayāya, oṃ vyauṃ śirase, oṃ huṃ kavacāya, oṃ īṃ śikhāyai, oṃ huṃ kavacāya, oṃ jyauṃ netrābhyām, oṃ phaṭ astrāya. [Offer] a tenth part for the limbs, and [worship] her whose face is like the full moon.
I worship Amṛteśvarī, who wears a crown of nectar, who has three eyes, and whose inner form rests upon the Lord of Nectar. Oṃ juṃ saḥ, obeisance to Amṛtalakṣmī.
(108) [One should perform] the limbs like the Lord of Nectar; at the end of the root mantra, "vauṣaṭ" is for the full oblation. Gu.
This is the *hyetitarpaṇa* (libation for the ancestors), the *nirodhārgha* (offering for cessation). O Śrī Mṛtyuñjaya, this is the great *camasa* vessel. The *gāyatrī* mantra for conquering death is:
*juṃ vī saḥ śa oṃ*. In the fire sacrifice (*homa*), [the deities] are the Moon and the Sun.
With large eyes and a smiling face, seated within two lotuses,
his hands radiant with the gestures (mudrās), the noose, the *svadhā* gesture, and a rosary;
possessing a complexion like the light of the moon, his body drenched in nectar falling from the head of Indra upon his crown, and adorned with necklaces—

I meditate upon Paśupati, the conqueror of death, who deludes the entire universe with the brilliance of his divine ornaments; [I offer] a flower into the fire, along with the water for invocation, the water for the feet, and so forth.
To Amṛteśa, whose body is the sky, [I offer] dhī; to Netra, [I offer] tanno. (3)
Oṃ juṃ saḥ haṃsaḥ māṃ pālaya (2). So haṃ saḥ juṃ oṃ (108).
Oṃ hṛ [heart], juṃ śi [head], saḥ śikhā [tuft], oṃ ka [armor], juṃ ne [eyes], saḥ astrā [weapon].
The ten-part [offering] for the limbs and the full offering [are performed] with [the mantra] "caṃdrodbhāsitasūrvajaṃsu."
Holding a vessel of the nectar of the nectar of poetry in his lotus-hand, with a stainless smile like ten million suns, having the sun, fire,
and moon as his eyes, and bearing a noose, a rosary, and a goad in his palms;

I meditate upon Paśupati, the compassionate Śiva, the conqueror of death (Mṛtyuñjaya). At the end of the root mantra, [one says] "vauṣaṭ"; this is the secret libation (tarpaṇa), and the offering of water (argha) is likewise restricted. [One meditates on] the God with three or five eyes, and so forth; the visualization (dhyāna) ends with the slightly terrifying-faced goddess Siddhāntā.

The flower for the fire is [offered] to Śrī Aghoreśvara Saṅkālāgnirudrabhairava; the meter is Anuṣṭubh; the deity is the Supreme Self in the form of Śrī Aghora; the seed-syllable is OṂ VĪ HŪṂ ŚA; perform the action (KURU). [This is] the application in the fire-oblation (HOMA).

Having offered the water for the feet (*pādya*) and other items from the *vidhi-argha* vessel with the *han* mantra and so forth, and having performed the placement of mantras (*vaktra-nyāsa*) upon one's own faces, [one recites]: "To the multiformed one, to the cave-eyed one;
may that which is terrible [protect us]—Oṃ Huṃ! To the non-terrible ones, and to the terrible ones, and to those more terrible than the terrible. (3) Oṃ Huṃ Aghorebhyaḥ Thaghorebhyaḥ Ghoratarebhyaḥ.
And to all the forms of Śarva, to all the Rudras from every direction, obeisance to you! *Huṃ*!
Obeisance, svāhā! (108) *Kṣaṃ*, svāhā to the face of Īśāna;
*Yaṃ*, svāhā to the face of Tatpuruṣa; *Raṃ*, svāhā to the face of Aghora.
LAṂ to the face of Sadyojāta, svāhā; VAṂ to the face of Vāmadeva, svāhā;
Aghorebhyaḥ sarvātmane hṛdayāya namaḥ svāhā;
then to the faces of the Ghoras, to the Brahma-head, to the head, svāhā; gho...
Oṃ *ra* to the most fierce ones, *gho* to the blazing crest, *ra* *vaṣaṭ* *svāhā*.
O *sarva*, to *sarva* everywhere, to *piṅgala*, to the armor, *huṃ* *svāhā*.
Oṃ *juṃ* *saḥ*, to the forms of light, to the eyes, *vauṣaṭ* *svāhā*.
"Hā! Salutation to your forms as Rudra; to the Pāśupata weapon, which is difficult to pierce;
to the Weapon-mantra, Phaṭ Svāhā! Then, one-tenth of the limbs [is offered]. Thereafter, the full oblation (pūrṇāhuti):
"O you who shine with a shield, a noose, and a staff adorned with a horn in your left hand..."

[He is] white as the moon, with a face like that of a young man, seated upon a deer; he bears a banner, a mallet, and a bell in his left hands, while in his right hands he holds an axe, an elephant-goad, a lotus-stalk, a hand-drum, a thunderbolt, a trident, and displays the gesture of fearlessness.

His consort has the luster of a cloud and holds a flag and a mallet. He stands upon a deer. *Note on terminology:* * *ṇāṃṭika* (variant of *nāṭika*): "young man" or "actor. * *vibhrāṇaṃ*: "bearing" or "carrying. * *dhvaja*: "banner. * *udgara*: "mallet" or "hammer. * *osvanibha*: "having the luster of a cloud" (*osva* = cloud; *nibha* = resembling). * *devy-aṅkaṃ*: "with the Goddess in his lap" or "embraced by the Goddess. * *kuṭhāraṃ*: "axe. * *dakṣe*: "in the right [hand]. * *aṅkuśa*: "elephant-goad. * *kandalī*: "lotus-stalk. * *ṣuḍamaru*: "hand-drum" (*ṣuḍ* = hand; *ḍamaru* = hand-drum). * *vajra*: "thunderbolt. * *triśūla*: "trident. * *abhaya*: "fearlessness" (the *abhaya-mudrā*). * *dudrasthaṃ*: "seated upon a deer" (*du* = deer; *drastha* = standing/seated). * *śaravaktraṃ*: "with a face like a young man" (*śara* = young man/arrow; *vaktra* = face). * *indu-dhava*: "white as the moon" (*indu* = moon; *dhava* = white).
We praise Laṃsvacchandanātha; with "Mūla-ante Vauṣaṭ," the full oblation is offered.
Now, I bow to Aghoreśvarī, the Supreme Brahman, the Sovereign Consort whose nature is consciousness, who transcends Brahmā and the other causal deities.

[Offer] a flower into the fire for the blissful Śivā. Oṃ vī hrīṃ śa kuru (2) kī; [perform] the invocation and other rites in the homa for the Supreme Self, whose nature is consciousness, the Sovereign Goddess Aghorī.
*Tatnaḥ śaktiḥ* (3). *Oṃ hrīṃ aghoreśvari huṃ phaṭ, aghoreśvaryai svāhā* (108). *Hāṃ hīṃ huṃ haiṃ hauṃ haḥ*, etc., for the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*).
One-tenth part (*daśāṃśa*) [of that]. *Kṣaṃ īśānavaktrāya svāhā*, etc., for the faces (*vaktra*).

The fivefold oblation is performed with the root mantra, followed by the full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*). Now, we praise the Absolute (*niṣkala*), whose form is the Supreme Light, the sole nature of the universe, the soul of the universe, and the cause of the creation and other processes of the universe— Svacchanda.
Bhairava is beyond the universe yet consists of the universe; he is joined with the eight Bhairavas, perfectly tranquil, partless, pure,
all-pervading, and stainless.
We worship that splendor which is the dense depth of consciousness, awakening, and bliss, the refuge of all; it is the supreme state of the *haṃsa* seated within the vital breath (*prāṇa*),
the support for those whose bodies possess subtle discernment, and the three and a half [units] of the breath.

He who, as Svacchandanaatha, the supreme deity, reverses those [energies] consisting of ten million by means of his mantra-nature— he, the supreme Bhairava, bestows the eternal, supreme splendor of his own body. [The ritual involves] flowers in the fire and the invocation (āvāhana).
[Recite] "To the Paramahaṃsa, the Mahāhaṃsa, may that Śiva be ours" (3).
[Then recite] "Oṃ Hūṃ, obeisance to Niṣkala Svacchandabhairava" (108 times). [And perform] the ten-part [recitation] beginning with "Hāṃ, obeisance to the Heart, Svāhā."
Or [one may offer] to the six limbs with "kṣuṃ īśānavaktrāya svāhā" and so forth;
or to Mā and the others with "svāhā," to Kapāleśa and the others with "svāhā," to the weapons such as the sword with "svāhā," and to the seven enclosures beginning with Kapāleśa with "svāhā."

*Oṃ nāgadevatābhyaḥ svāhā*. With the visualization "Vāme kheṭakaḥ," [the offering] is complete. At the end of the root mantra, *vauṣaṭ*. May the Lord of the Skanda-bhalli, together with the Goddess, his limbs, and his retinue, be pleased; may he be gratified. May there be satisfaction through this libation (*tarpaṇa*).
"O Snu, be present"— this is the *nirodha-argha* (obstructive offering).
Now, may there be prosperity for the Lord, who is marked by right arms holding a conch, mace, lotus, and discus, and by left arms holding a book, a mirror, a lotus bud, and a water-pot.

Now I praise the omnipresent Lord Śrī Vāsudeva, the granter of boons, who is ever resplendent with his consort Lakṣmī, who is mounted upon Garuḍa, who is the supreme object of compassion for his devotees, and who is marked by Lakṣmī as half of his own body.
Of this [Lord], Śrī Lakṣmī...
Sudeva, Nārada, Gāyatrī meter; Śrī Lakṣmī is the deity;
Śrīṃ is the seed syllable, Hrīṃ the power, and Oṃ the crest. For the fire-oblation (homa), [the mantra is] "Oṃ Vāsudevāya Lakṣmyai" for the invocation, the water for the feet (pādya), and so forth.
For the fulfillment of that, may Viṣṇu [grant it] to us: (3) Oṃ huṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Lakṣmīvāsudeva, the divine one. (108) Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Mahālakṣmī.
(108) Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the heart, which is the true essence of pure knowledge.

Svāhā! Oṃ hrīṃ, to the embodiment of all sovereign qualities, svāhā to the head. Oṃ hūṃ, to the one possessing all power, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock. Oṃ hraiṃ, to the one whose form is infinite strength, huṃ svāhā to the armor. Hrauṃ a...
*Parimitatejasenetrebhyo vauṣaṭ svāhā*. *Oṃ hraḥ apratihatavīryāya astrāya phaṭ svāhā*. Then, the full [offering]:
the mirror of the lotus of knowledge, filled with the jar of nectar.
I bow to the one whose hands are beautified by the supreme Sudarśana [discus], who shines with the splendor of the moonlight of Lakṣmī, who is the very essence of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa,
and who is the undivided form of the Self; [the mantra is] *mūla-ante vauṣaṭ*.

The offering for the rite of obstruction (*nirodhārgha*) is with the mantra "tarpaṇaṃ sannidhatsva. Then, [he offers] to Annapaṭi: delicious food placed in a silver vessel, consisting of curd and sugar-candy, held gracefully in his right hand along with a water-pot.
Meditate upon Vāmana for you— him who holds a vessel filled with nectar in his left hand and who abandons all worldly suffering. For this [hymn],
the Seer (ṛṣi) is Indu, the metre (chandas) is Virāṭ, and the deity is Śrī Dadhivāhana.

The application (*viniyoga*) of the mental deities is in the fire-oblation (*homa*). [Offer] a flower in the fire; [perform] the invocation (*āvāhana*), the water for the feet (*pādya*), and so forth. To Vāsudeva, to Nārāyaṇa:
"May Viṣṇu protect us" (RV 1.22.20). *Oṃ namo viṣṇave surapataye mahābā*...
Lāyānnaṃdehi svāhā (108). Oṃ namo hṛdayāya namaḥ svāhā.
Oṃ viṣṇave śirase svāhā. Oṃ surapataye śikhāyai vaṣaṭ svāhā. Oṃ mahābalāya kavacaṃ...

*cāyahuṃ svāhā*, give food! (2) *netrebhyo vauṣaṭ svāhā svāhā*, protect me with *phaṭ* svāhā! [I bow to] the one who is full, liberated, fair-complexioned, adorned with beautiful ornaments of fresh jewels, seated upon the moon, and having the form of a bee.
Worship Him whose lotus-face is beautified by a multitude of rays, who holds in His two lotus-hands a golden pitcher filled with pure water,
and who bears food placed upon a silver vessel, endowed with supreme qualities.

*Maḥ*, at the end of the root mantra *vauṣaṭ*, [is used for] the libation (*tarpaṇa*) and the obstructive offering (*nirodhārgha*). Then one should offer the three full oblations (*pūrṇā*). That which arises from the opening and closing of the eyes certainly undergoes destruction; indeed, that which begins with Brahmā is the cause.

This earth, fire, wind, and water are bound by the five-fold Māyā-noose; yet that Great Light, known as Niṣkala (the Partless), is eternally bound by the noose of Māyā and the rest, which consists of the five Kalās, and is devoid of all parts and divisions. Oṃ juṃ.

May there be satisfaction for the entire wheel of mantras: *astu vauṣaṭ*. [I bow to] Śaṅkara, who has five faces, who bestows boons, whose vehicle is the king of bulls, who bears the Gaṅgā, who is independent, whose mass of matted hair is adorned with a crescent moon and a garland of human skulls; [and] Brahmā...

We bow to you, whose pair of lotus feet destroy the cycle of time, who are partless, the bestower of all desired boons, and the destroyer of the fear of worldly existence—Oṃ Huṃ Bhairava, may there be nourishment for you; Svāhā! (2) Peace.
Seated in the lotus posture, wearing a moon-crested crown, five-faced and three-eyed,
he holds in his right hands a trident, a vajra, a sword, an axe, and the gesture of fearlessness,
while in his left hands he holds a serpent, a noose, a bell, together with a ḍamaru drum, and a goad.

I bow to Maheśa, who is adorned with the crescent moon, whose face is like a crystal orb, and who is the witness of all; Oṃ Huṃ, may I fulfill any deficiency or excess in the ritual procedure, Vauṣaṭ. (3) Then follows the libation with the remnants.
One should preserve the clarified butter for the purpose of the oblation to the deities.
Now follows the oblation of barley and sesame seeds; therein, first is the Vyāhṛti-homa:
*oṃ bhūḥ svāhā*, *oṃ bhuvaḥ svāhā*, *oṃ svaḥ svāhā*, *oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ*...
Oṃ bhūr svāhā. Oṃ bhuvaḥ svāhā.
Oṃ svaḥ svāhā. Oṃ mahaḥ svāhā. Oṃ janaḥ svāhā.
Oṃ tapaḥ svāhā. Oṃ satyaṃ svāhā. Now, the meditation on the Gāyatrī.

In the *Prapañcasāra*, [the Lord] has a body variegated by twenty-four syllables, with faces like the *mandāra* flower, yellow pigment (*rocanā*), collyrium (*añjana*), and the *japā* flower; with mouths like the moon, gems, and rising pearls; and possessing the qualities of the lotus, the discus, and the sword.

Holding a skull, a bow, a noose, a goad, and displaying the gestures of granting boons (*iṣṭa*) and fearlessness (*abhīta*), may she be the savior who delivers us from worldly existence and fulfills our desires. [Offer] flowers into the fire;
[perform] the invocation (*āvāhana*), the water for the feet (*pādya*), and so forth; [then perform] the internal placement (*nyāsa*) within oneself with *oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ*.
* tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt | oṃ svāhā || (108) || vā || (54) || vā || (27) || vā || (14) || vā || (7) || oṃ tat savituḥ hṛdayāya namaḥ svāhā ||
Hā vareṇyam śirase svāhā; bhargo devasya śikhāyai vaṣaṭ svāhā; dhīmahi kavacāya huṃ svāhā;
dhiyo yo naḥ netrebhyaḥ vauṣaṭ svāhā; pracodayāt.

*Tat astrāya phaṭ svāhā*. One-tenth of the limbs (*aṅga*) [is offered]. With the meditation on "pearls, coral... (*muktā-vidruma...*), the *pūrṇā* [offering] is performed. At the end of the root mantra, *vauṣaṭ* [is uttered]. *Tarpaṇam* (the libation). *Sannidhatsva* (be present) is the *nirodha-argha* (the obstructive offering). Then, Gaṇeśa...

One should perform an oblation of *dīnārya* and sesame seeds while meditating on Indra, the king, who wields the thunderbolt (*vajra*), has many eyes, is mounted upon Airāvaṇa, and is surrounded by auspicious apsarases;
[the mantra is]: "Oṃ, salutation to Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt. Vī.
One should meditate upon Agni, who is seated on a goat, holding a sacrificial ladle (*kūrca*), a water-pot (*aṅkuśa*), a rosary, and a spear, and who is tawny with tawny eyes. [The mantra is:
*Raṃ*, obeisance to Agni, who holds a spear in his hand. One should likewise meditate upon Yama, who holds a staff.

O fair-faced one, one should likewise meditate upon Nairṛti, the lord of the pretas, who is wrathful, seated upon a buffalo, holding a noose in his hand, the destroyer of obstacles, and bearing a staff in his hand; salutations to him. Similarly, O lady of excellent countenance, one should meditate upon Yama, who holds a sword in his hand.

For the pacification of all obstacles, [I bow] to Bhīma, the lord of the Kṣas, with the syllable *kṣaṃ*; to Nirṛti, who holds a sword in his hand, with the syllable *yaṃ*; and to Varuṇa, the lord of the waters, who is white in color, seated upon a fish, and holds a noose in his hand, in the western direction.

One should meditate upon Vāyu, the supreme protector through fire-oblations, who holds a noose in his hand— *vaṃ*— and salutations to Varuṇa; one should meditate upon Vāyu, clad in yellow garments, possessing a smoky banner and moving swiftly,
seated upon a deer for the sake of protection and the dispeller of all obstacles— *yaṃ*— or *vā*.

One should remember with devotion the Lord of Yakṣas, who holds a banner in his hand, is mounted upon a ram, is yellow in color, rides a man, and wields a mace, for the sake of attaining the fulfillment of dharma, kāma, and artha—namely, to Kuvera, the wielder of the mace. Homage! To him who is mounted on a ram, whose hand holds a mace, who is yellow, and whose vehicle is a man. One should remember the Lord of Yakṣas with devotion for the attainment of dharma, kāma, and artha—to Kuvera, the wielder of the mace. Homage! To him who has a banner in his hand. Homage! To him who is mounted on a ram, whose hand holds a mace, who is yellow, and whose vehicle is a man. One should remember the Lord of Yakṣas with devotion for the attainment of the success of dharma, kāma, and artha—to Kuvera, the wielder of the mace. Homage! To him who has a banner in his hand. One should remember the Lord of Yakṣas with devotion for the attainment of the success of dharma, kāma, and artha—to Kuvera, the wielder of the mace. Homage! To him who has a banner in his hand. Homage! To him who is mounted on a ram, whose hand holds a mace, who is yellow, and whose vehicle is a man. One should remember the Lord of Yakṣas with devotion for the attainment of the success of dharma, kāma, and artha—to Kuvera, the wielder of the mace. Homage! To him who has a banner in his hand. Homage! To him who is mounted on a ram, whose hand holds a mace, who is yellow, and whose vehicle is a man. One should remember the Lord of Yakṣas with devotion for the attainment of the success of dharma, kāma, and artha—to Kuvera, the wielder of the mace. Homage! To him who has a banner in his hand. Homage! To him who is mounted on a ram, whose hand holds a mace, who is yellow, and whose vehicle is a man. One should remember the Lord of Yakṣas with devotion for the attainment of the success of dharma, kāma, and artha—to Kuvera, the wielder of the mace. Homage! To him who has a banner in his hand. Homage! To him who is mounted on a ram, whose hand holds a mace, who is yellow, and whose vehicle is a man. One should remember the Lord of Yakṣas with devotion for the attainment of the success of dharma, kāma, and artha—to Kuvera, the wielder of the mace. Homage! To him who has a banner in his hand. Homage! To him who is mounted on a ram, whose hand holds a mace, who is yellow, and whose vehicle is a man. One should remember the Lord of Yakṣas with devotion for the attainment of the success of dharma, kāma, and artha—to Kuvera, the wielder of the mace. Homage! To him who has a banner in his hand. Homage! To him who is mounted on a ram, whose hand holds a mace, who is yellow, and whose vehicle is a man. One should remember the Lord of Yakṣas with devotion for the attainment of the success of dharma, kāma, and artha—to Kuvera, the wielder of the mace. Homage! To him who has a banner in his hand. Homage! To him who is mounted on a ram, whose hand holds a mace, who is yellow, and whose vehicle is a man. One should remember the Lord of Yakṣas with devotion for the attainment of the success of dharma, kāma, and artha—to Kuvera, the wielder of the mace. Homage! To him who has a banner in his hand. Homage! To him who is mounted on a ram, whose hand holds a mace, who is yellow, and whose vehicle is a man. Homage! To him who is mounted on a ram, whose hand holds a mace, who is yellow, and whose vehicle is a man.
