Having worshipped the accomplishment of mastery (*vaśitvasiddhi*) and the Sarvonmādinī mudrā at their two sides, one should display the Sarvonmādinī mudrā;
these are the Kula-kaula yoginīs in the Sarvārthasādhaka cakra.

"May those who have been conquered be satisfied"—thus is the fifth enclosure. (2) *Hrīṃ Klīṃ Nluṃ*, obeisance to the wheel that effects all protection. (2) Obeisance to the Nigarbha Yoginīs within the inner ten-spoked [wheel]. (2) *Maṃ*, obeisance to the feet of the Goddess Sarvajñā. (0)
(2) Yaṃ—the goddess who bestows all powers; (2) Raṃ—the goddess who bestows all sovereignty;
(2) Laṃ—the goddess who consists of all knowledge; (2) Vaṃ—the goddess who destroys all diseases;
(2) Śaṃ—the goddess whose nature is the support of all; (2) Ṣaṃ—the goddess of all... [text truncated]
The goddess Pāpaharā (2), the goddess Saṃsarvānandamayī (2), the goddess Haṃsarvarakṣāsvarūpiṇī (2), and the goddess Laṃsarvepsitaphalapradā—
these are to be worshipped in the inner ten-spoked wheel in reverse order starting from the west.

Yet, having worshipped the Great Goad Mudrā (Mahāṅkuśa-mudrā) in front of the venerable Śrīpāda, the Mistress of the Wheel of the Triple City Garland (Tripuramālinī-cakreśvarī), who is all-knowing, and on both her sides, one should display the Great Goad Mudrā. These...

"May the Nigarbha Yoginīs in the Sarvarakṣākara-cakra be worshipped and satisfied"—thus is the sixth enclosure. (2) Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Sauḥ, obeisance to the Sarvarogahara-cakra. (2) Obeisance to the Rahasya Yoginīs.
On the eight-spoked [wheel]: (2) AṂ ĀṂ (16) RAVALŪṂ VAŚINĪVĀGDEVATĀŚRĪPĀ (0) (2) KAṂ (5) KALHĪṂ KĀMEŚVARĪVĀGDEVATĀ (2) CAṂ (5) NAVALĪṂ MODINĪVĀGDEVATĀ (2) ṬAṂ (5) YALARTHAṂ VIMALĀVĀGDE...
Vatāśrīpā (2) Taṃ (5) Jamarī Aruṇā Vāgdevatā Śrīpā (0) (2) Paṃ (5) Hasalavaya Rthaṃ Jayinī Vāgdevatā Śrīpā (2) Yaṃ (4) Jhamaraya Rthaṃ Sarveśvarī Vāgdevatā Śrīpā (2) Śaṃ.

(4) One should worship [the goddesses] in the eight-spoked [cakra], starting from the west and proceeding in reverse order: Kṣamarī, Kaulinī, Vāgdevatā, and Śrīpā. Then, one should worship Mūla, Tripurāsiddhā, Cakreśvarī, and Śrīpā; and in front of Vaśinī, those two [should be worshipped] for the sake of worldly enjoyment.
Having worshipped the *siddhi* and the *khecarīmudrā*, one should display the *khecarīmudrā*. [One should say:
"May these secret yoginīs in the wheel that removes all diseases be worshipped and gratified. Here, in the sixth and seventh [sections]...
The transposition of the syllables is to be understood according to the different tantras. This concludes the seventh enclosure.
Now, outside the triangle: *yāṃ rāṃ lāṃ vāṃ śāṃ drāṃ drīṃ klīṃ nluṃ saḥ, namaḥ to all the arrows that cause expansion*.

(2) *Namaḥ* to the bow for the purpose of deluding all; (2) *Hrīṃ Āṃ*, *namaḥ* to the noose for the purpose of bringing all under control; (2) *Kroṃ Kroṃ*, *namaḥ* to the goad for the purpose of paralyzing all. Thus [are the mantras] for the positions of the Goddess's arms.

In the Kādima system, because the worship of the Nityās is established in the four directions beginning with the West, there is no such conceptualization here; consequently, this enclosure (*āvaraṇa*) is absent due to the lack of a location for the circle of the Mistress of the Circle (*cakreśvarī-cakra*) within this observance (*samaya*).

According to the *Itikādimate*, one should worship [the deity] in the space between Malā and Ajayinī; however, as stated below according to the *Nityātantra*, it is said to be "just as it is. Here, some maintain that after the worship of the weapons (*āyudha*), the goddesses of the limbs (*aṅgadevyas*) are to be worshipped.

Others say that after worshipping the Goddess in the center, one should worship the limb-deities (aṅgadevatās) outside the triangle; then, once the worship of the enclosures (āvaraṇas) has commenced, the weapon-deities (āyudhadevatās) are to be worshipped outside the limb-deities according to the stated sequence.
The tradition of the oral transmission (*upahvara-saṃpradāya*) holds that the deities are worshipped within the body at the beginning and end.
At this very time, one should worship the fifteen previously mentioned Nityā goddesses within the body; such is the *Kādimata*. Thus ends [the section].

Prior to the worship of the battle (*raṇapūjā*), one should [worship] the breasts of the Goddess within the lines of the triangle according to the *Nityātantra* and other texts: (2) *HA SA RAḤ HA SA KA LA RĪṂ HA SA RAUḤ SARVASIDDHIPRADACAKRĀYA NAMAḤ* (2). Parā.
Salutation to the Yoginīs of the supreme secret. Keīla Hrīṃ!

In the fire-wheel (*agnicakra*) at the sacred seat (*pīṭha*) of Kāmarūpa, which is the essence of Mitreśanātha and the presiding deity of the state of birth (*jāgrat*), [I bow] to the one whose nature is the power of will (*icchāśakti*) and who is Rudra himself.

O Śaktikāmeśvarī Devī, at the tip of the glorious triangle (2), *hasakalahalahrīṃ*, in the solar wheel (*sūryacakra*) at the sacred seat (*pīṭha*) of Jālandhara, O Sovereign of the Sixth [Planet] (*ṣaṣṭīśanātha*),
O presiding deity of the dream state (*svapnadaśādhiṣṭhāyaka*), O Wisdom [Energy] (*jñānaśa*)...

O Śrī Vajreśvarī Devī, whose nature is action (*kriyā*), who possesses the power of the Self, in the left triangle [of the heart], in the *sakala* moon-wheel of *hrīṃ*, in the Pīṭha of Pūrṇagiri which is the essence of Uḍḍīśanātha, presiding over the state of deep sleep (*suṣupti*).
One should worship the Śrīpāda of the Goddess Ālinī— who embraces the Bhaga of the power of the Self which consists of the power of action— in the reverse order starting from the West;
one should worship in the triangle— this is the Kādimata, the root of Tripurā.
Having worshipped Cakreśvarī-Śrīpāda in front of Kāmeśvarī and on her two sides,
and having worshipped Icchāsiddhi and Vījamudrā, one should display the Vījamudrā. These are the Parāpara-Rahasya Yoginīs, who grant all [attainments].
"May those worshipped and gratified in the wheel that bestows supernatural powers (*iddhi*) be satisfied"—thus is the eighth enclosure.
*Mūla* (root mantra), "Salutation to the Wheel Consisting Entirely of Bliss.
*Mūla*, "Salutation to the Yoginīs of the Ultimate Secret"—thus in the lunar [enclosure].

(2) I worship and bow to the Śrīpādukā of the Goddess Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, the Supreme Brahman, the Self-power (*ātma-śakti*), who presides over the state of radiance (*sphurattā*) within the essence of Mūlādhāra, Uḍyāna, Pīṭha, Carya, and Ānanda. (3) [Worship] at the Bindu.

One should conquer the root-mantra of the sovereign of the Śrī Mahātripurasundarī-cakra. Having worshipped the Śrīpādukā at the very center and the Siddhi of Attainment (Prāpti-siddhi) on its two sides, as well as the Yoni-mudrā, one should display the Yoni-mudrā. These...

All the secret Yoginīs reside in the Great Cakra consisting of universal bliss, within the lunar sphere; there dwells the Supreme Nectar-Power (Parāmṛta-śakti), the Sovereign of all sacred seats (Pīṭheśvarī), the Sovereign of all mantras (Mantra-īśvarī),
the Sovereign of the entire universe (Viśveśvarī), the Sovereign of all speech (Vāgīśvarī), and the mistress of the whole world.

May the venerable Mahātripurasundarī— along with her retinue, her [eight] mothers of manifestation (*utpattimātṛkā*), her wheels (*cakra*), her weapons (*āyudha*), her mudrās, her attendants (*vāhana*), and her entourage—
be worshipped and gratified through the supreme, the lower, and the intermediate modes of worship.
"Namaḥ"—thus ends the ninth enclosure (*āvaraṇa*).

In all these instances, some according to the oral tradition (*sampradāya*) desire that before the words "I worship the sandals" (*pādukāṃ pūjayāmi*), the word *śrī* (Glorious One) or in some cases the word *śakti* (Power) be inserted. However, in the *Kādimata*, it is [the word *kā*].
In the triad beginning with Īśvarī, the words *Śrī* and *Devī* are to be understood according to the traditional transmission (*saṃpradāya*). Likewise, in the case of Mahātripurasundarī,
one should apply the pair of words *Mahat* and *Śrī*, as well as the word *Devī*, in the ninth wheel (*cakra*).
The *Manoramā* states that the word "Great" (*mahat*) alone is to be understood here, and not anything else.

Thus, in the case of the nine *cakreśvarīs* beginning with Tripurā, one should not apply the two seed-syllables (*bīja*) nor the term "*cakreśvarī*"; rather, [one should use] the root mantra (*mūla*).

In my tradition, one should employ the two words "Śrī" in the ritual formula beginning with "Tripurānityā-śrī-pādukām," and so forth. According to the oral tradition, [the name] is Subhagānandanātha; the mantra for the offering is as follows: amu...

The mantra "May he accept this worship with the *kaca* and *krep*" should be employed; the remainder is to be understood as previously stated. [Thus ends the sixth ray in the *Subhagārcāratna*, engraved by Āgamirāmacandra. Now, with the previously mentioned limb-mantras (*aṅgamantra*s)...

One should worship the limbs of the Goddess's body with this eight-syllable mantra of the Self: *Oṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ so'haṃ svāhā*. Having worshipped thus, one should perform sacrifice with the *bhūta-mantras* as follows: *ā ek ca ṭa ta pa ya śa praṇa śa*.
Kti-Śrīpā; Iī-Ai-Kha-Ṭa-Tha-Ra-Ṣa-Agni-Śakti-Śrīpā; Uū-O-Ga-Ḍa-Da-Va-La-Śilā-Śakti-Śrīpā; ṚṜau-Ca-Jha-Ḍha-Dha-Bha-Va-Ha-Amvu-Śakti-Śrīpā; ḶḸaṃ-Jha-Ña.
One should worship that [deity] as the body of the Goddess, namely "Ṇa-na-ma-ha-ka-śa-kti-śrī-pā";

this is the view of the *Tantrarāja*. Furthermore, in the *Nityātantra-saṃhitā* and other texts, the worship of the five pentads (*pañcapañcikā*) is taught, which is as follows: having uttered the root mantra, [one worships] in the Great Treasury (*mahākośa*).
Seated upon a throne adorned with a multitude of bees, the Great Tripurasundarī, the progenitor of all auspiciousness, [is] the venerable feet [of the Goddess]. Oṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ so 'haṃ svāhā paṃ.
Obeisance to the venerable feet of the Great Supreme Light-Casket of the multitude of Cakośeśvarīs;
Obeisance to the venerable feet of the Supreme Niṣkala Śāmbarī, the Mahākośeśvarī (Oṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Sauḥ);
[obeisance] to the venerable feet of the Unborn Haṃsa-Kośeśvarī.
Having uttered the entire Mātṛkā from *pā* to *śrīpā*, [and] *aṃ āṃ* [to] *mahākośeśvarīmātṛkāśrīpā*— these are the five Kośa-vidyās.
Having uttered the root [mantra], [the mantra of] Mahākalpalateśvarī...
Seated upon a throne adorned with gems, the mother of all good fortune,
the illustrious Mahātripurasundarī, [her] Śrīpāda: Oṃ hrīṃ huṃ kha cha cha kṣaḥ strīṃ huṃ kṣe hrīṃ phaṭ, the Sovereign of the Great Kalpalatā, Tvaritā.
Śrīpā Oṃ Hrīṃ Ha Sa Ka Ha La Hrīṃ Hrīṃ Oṃ, obeisance to Sarasvatī.
Śrīpā (0), O Sovereign of the Great Kalpa-creeper, O Sovereign of the Pārijāta tree!
Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ, O Sovereign of the Great Kalpa-creeper, Tripura...
Ṭā śrīpā (0) drāṃ drīṃ klīṃ kluṃ saḥ mahākalpalateśvarī pañcavāṇeśī śrīpā (0). Thus are the five Kalpalatās.
Having uttered the root mantra, [one worships] Mahālakṣmīśvarī adorned by the multitude [of deities].
Seated upon a lotus, the mother of all auspiciousness, Mahātripurasundarī Śrīpādukā;
Śrīṃ Lakṣmīśvarī Śrīpādukā (0); Oṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kamale Kamalālaye Prasīda (2) Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ.

Oṃ, salutation to Mahālakṣmī. Oṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ Klīṃ, to the venerable feet of the Sovereign Goddess Mahālakṣmī, the Mistress of the Three Powers. Śrīṃ Sahakalahrīṃ Śrīṃ, to the venerable feet of the Sovereign Goddess Mahālakṣmī of Universal Sovereignty.
Having recited the root mantra *PĀ*— the Vidyā of the Sovereign Mahālakṣmīśvarī—
one should worship the venerable feet of Mahātripurasundarī, the mother of all auspiciousness, who is seated upon a throne adorned by the assembly of Mahāratneśvarīs.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ namo bhagavati māheśvari annapūrṇe svāhā | Mahāratneśvarī annapūrṇā śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi | Aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ | Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ namo bhagavate mātaṅgeśvarāya...
O you who captivate the minds of all beings, O you who bring all kings under control, O you who bring all the worlds under control, *Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ Aiṃ*, O Mahāratneśvarī Mātaṅgī,
[obeisance to] the feet of Śrī; *Hrīṃ*, O Mahāratneśvarī Bhuvaneśvarī, Śrī.

Pā Aiṃ Glau Aiṃ, obeisance to the Blessed One, Vārtālī Vārāhī (2), O boar-faced one! O you who blind, obeisance to you, the blinder! O you who obstruct, obeisance to you, the obstructor! O you who crush, obeisance to you, the crusher! O you who delude, obeisance to you, the deluder! O you who paralyze!
O Stambhini, salutations! Aiṃ Glauṃ Aiṃ! Paralyze the speech, mind, eyes, mouth, enemies, and tongues of all those who are wicked or extremely wicked! Śī.

*Ghraṃ vaśyaṃ kuru* (2) *aiṃ glauṃ aiṃ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ huṃ phaṭ svāhā mahāratneśvarīvārāhīśrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ*. Thus are the five-jewel mantras (*pañcaratnavidyā*). Having recited the root mantra, [worship] the host of Mahākāmadugheśvarīs.
Seated upon the adorned throne, the mother of all auspiciousness,
the venerable Mahātripurasundarī— *śrīpā*, *hrīṃ*, *haṃsaḥ*, *saṃjīvini*, *juṃ*, *jīvaṃ*, make [this] reside in the knot of the vital breaths (*prāṇagranthi*), *saḥ svāhā*, the Great One.
O Sovereign of the Wish-Fulfilling Cow, O Sovereign of Nectar, O Śrīpā! Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ! Speak, speak, O Goddess of Speech! Hsaiṃ! O you who are moistened and overflowing, cause great agitation!
Hasakalarīṃ Oṃ! Grant liberation! Hsauṃ! O Great Wish-Fulfilling Cow!
Śvarīsudhāsūśrīpāda, Aiṃ Amṛteśvarī, Amṛtavarṣiṇī,
Amṛtaṃ srāvaya (2), Hrīṃ Jūṃ Saḥ Svāhā Mahākāmadugheśvarī Amṛteśī Śrīpāda, Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ Namaḥ Bha.

*Gavati-māheśvari annapūrṇe svāhā mahākāmadugheśvarī annapūrṇā-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi*. Thus, these are the five wish-granting cows (*pañcakāmadughāḥ*) [and] the excellent second wish-granting creeper (*kalpalatā*). This is from the *Nityātantra*.

In the *Hitā* [Tantra], as previously stated, the second *Ratnavidyā*, namely *Siddhalakṣmī*, is to be understood as being in the state of a *Saṃhitā*, [and] as being "almost complete" (*sannapūrṇā*) due to the distinction of the mantra; thus ends the worship of the five pentads (*pañcapañcikā*). *Aiṃ klīṃ*.
Sauḥ! To the east, on the lion-throne, the Vidyā Tripureśvarī Śrīpādukā;
Hrīṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ (2), Klīṃ (2), Hasakalīṃ Sauḥ! On the southern lion-throne, the Vidyās Lalitā, Kāmeśvarī, and Raktanetrā Śrī...

Pā Hrīṃ Haṃsaḥ, O Saṃjīvini, make me live, O Jīva; place [me] within the knot of life! Saḥ Svāhā, speak! Speak, O Goddess of Speech! Niḥ Saiṃ Klinne Kledini Aiṃ Kroṃ Nityamadadrave Hrīṃ (2) Hasare Hasakala.
RĪṂ, the Vidyā Sañjīvanī on the western lion-throne;
Mṛtyuñjayā, Vajraprastāriṇī, Tripurabhairavī, Pā (0) HSAIṂ HASAKALĪṂ HSAUṂ; the Vidyā Āḍāmara on the northern lion-throne.
Having uttered the root mantra of Reśvarabhairavīpāda, [one recites] "Śrī Mahātripurasundarīpā" in the bindu;
these are the five lion-throne vidyās: *hsrīṃ mahhrīṃ śrīṃ kalahrīṃ pū*.
The feet of the Goddess Unmanā, the Sovereign of the Eastern Tradition (Pūrvāmnāya), at the triangle within the square and the bindu:
*aiṃ klīṃ ne klīṃ madadrave kule hsauḥ*.
The feet of the Goddess Bhoginī, the Sovereign of the Southern Tradition (Dakṣiṇāmnāya), at the fourteen [spokes].
In the triangle of Rādi, within the *bindu*, [are the syllables]: vaiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hasa khaphreṃ hsauḥ;
obeisance to the Blessed Lady, hasa khaphreṃ hsauḥ.

Salutations to the Blessed One, Kubjikā, *hasakhaphreṃ*, *kṣāṃ hrīṃ huṃ*, O terrible one, O most terrible one, O you whose face is not terrible! *chāṃ chīṃ kiṇi* (twice), *viśve hasauḥ hasakhaphreṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ*, Sovereign of the Western Tradition (*paścimāmnāyeśvarī*).
One should worship Kubjikādevī-pā (0), Ha Sa Kha Phreṃ Mahācaṇḍayogeśvarī, Uttarāmnāyeśvarī, and Kālikā-pā (0) at every *cakra* or in the *bindu*. This is the *āmnāya*-worship: Oṃ Tāre Uttā...
*Resvāhā*, salutation to the Vaiṣṇava doctrine;
in the square [mandala], having uttered *Gāyatrī*, salutation to the Brāhma doctrine; in the sixteen-petaled and eight-petaled [mandalas], *Ghṛṇiḥ Sūrya Āditya Oṃ*, salutation to the Saura doctrine.
On the fourteen-spoked [wheel]: *oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya vaiṣṇavadarśanāya namaḥ*. On the two ten-spoked [wheels]: *hrīṃ śāktadarśanāya namaḥ*.
On the eight-cornered [wheel]: *oṃ namaḥ śivāya śivadarśanāya namaḥ*.
Maḥ. Regarding the triangle (*tryaśra*):

according to the *Vāmakeśvaratantra*, the sequence of philosophical systems (*darśana*) in the *Nityātantra* is Śaiva, Śākta, Brāhma, Vaiṣṇava, Saura, and Bauddha. [The triangle] is the reflection of the lunar orb.
The sequence of locations for the two left-hand parts— the wheel of emanation (*sṛṣṭicakra*) and the wheel of maintenance (*sthiticakra*)—

consists of the three [cakras] beginning with *vinmumukhāṇi*. The wheel of withdrawal (*saṃhāracakra*) consists of the three [cakras] beginning with the inner ten-spoked one (*antardaśāra*), and the wheel of maintenance (*sthiticakra*) consists of the eight-spoked one (*aṣṭāra*).
The three [offerings] beginning with *prabhṛti* are known as the "Wheel of Emanation" (*sṛṣṭicakra*).
Next is the worship of the four commitments (*catussamaya-pūjā*). Having first uttered the Nityā Kāmeśvarī as previously described, [one offers] to the commitment-deity (samayadevatā) of Kāmeśvarī.

One should worship Tivaiṇdavā in front; having uttered the previously mentioned Vajreśvarī-nityā, one should worship the Samaya-deity Vajreśvarī with "Vajreśvarī-samayadevatāyai" on the left side of the goddess Tivaiṇdavā; [and] the previously mentioned Bhagamālinī...
Having recited the *nityā*, one should worship the *samaya* deity Bhagamālinī with "Śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi" to the right of the goddess Vaindava; then, having recited the root mantra (*mūla*),
[one worships] the *samaya* deity Mahātripurasundarī.

Then, at the feet of Śrīpā [the venerable goddess], one should offer *hrīṃ śrīṃ* to these: the Prakaṭa (Manifest), Gupta (Secret), Guptarata (Secret-Love), Saṃpradāya (Tradition), Kulakaula, Nigarbha (Womb), Rahasya (Secret), Parāpararahasya (Secret of the Higher and Lower), Atirahasya (Supremely Secret) Yoginīs, and Śrīpā [the venerable goddess]. Thus [ends the section].

Having gratified the worshipful one with the root mantra and honored him with the fivefold offerings (*pañcopacāra*), one should offer flowers and water and perform the royal services (*rājopacāra*). Therein,
having recollected the *ṛṣi* and so forth, and taking up the rosary, one should meditate upon the Goddess as the embodiment of the *kāmakalā*.
If one recites [the mantra] according to one's capacity, having remembered the Ṛṣi and so forth, one should offer the recitation (japa) into the hand of the Goddess held in the left hand.
However, in the Kādimata system, one should recite it one thousand times; this is the primary ritual procedure (mukhya-kalpa). [This is the twenty-first [chapter].]
Eighty-four [units] is the middling [size], and one hundred is the last; then,

having sprinkled the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) or the sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila), or the vessel, with the arghya water from the third section of the Vidyā and the daily Nityā-mantras using kuśa grass, [one should proceed].

Having drawn four lines with their tips pointing east and north, one should take the fire from the third section of the Vidyā and the daily Nityā in the central square there, [reciting] "Obeisance to the flesh-eaters" (kravyādebhyaḥ namaḥ) toward the south.
In that direction, having set aside the portion for the flesh-eaters (kravyāda),

having consecrated the third section with the daily deities of the day by means of *kuśa* grass, having strewn it around, and having brought the Goddess into the fire, one should worship her with the root mantra and the third part of the Vidyā.
One should offer oblations preceded by the recollection of the tongues [of fire], which are enumerated as follows:
Hiraṇyā, Gaganā, Raktā, Kṛṣṇā, Āsu-prabhā, Bahurūpā, and Atiraktā. Regarding these tongues: [the offering is to be made].
Then, according to the sequence of worship, having offered oblations sixteen times to all the deities of the enclosures and to the Goddess, and having worshipped them,
one should recite the mantra a number of times equal to the oblations offered and join it between the eyebrows, which are the abode of the light of the drop (*bindu*).
The homa as described by Itikādima is for the *Nityātantra* and the *Saṃhitā*. However,

in the case of the *Tantrasaṃhitā*, one should first install and worship the Goddess in the fire as before, offer five oblations with the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*), and then give six oblations with the mantras of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga-mantra*).
This is the *itinityahoma*. Then, in front of the Śrīcakra, one should offer a *bali* to Kurukullā alone with water containing other side-dishes, [reciting]:
*Kurukullāyā oṃ kurukulle hrīṃ mama sarvajanaṃ vaśam ānaya hoṃ*.
Svāhā! (1) To Kurukullā: Oṃ Kurukulle Hrīṃ Svāhā!
(2) Oṃ Kurukulle Svāhā! (3) Having offered the bali with these three [mantras] in the four corners beginning with the northeast (īśāna), [one should proceed].
Having drawn four mandalas in sequence— square, triangular,
and circular— with the knees touching the ground, [one should worship] with "Oṃ hrīṃ to the pervasive mandala" and "Oṃ namaḥ."
Having performed the worship, one should offer the bali-oblation to Vaṭuka, the Yoginīs, the Kṣetrapālas, and the Gaṇeśas with the following mantra:
"Come, come, O Son of the Goddess, Vaṭukanātha,
resplendent with a mass of tawny matted hair!"

"O you whose face is the flame of the three eyes, destroy all obstacles; accept this offering along with all ritual services, svāhā!"— with this mantra, [one should offer] using the index finger together with the thumb.
One should offer the bali-oblation to Vaṭuka, whether he be above the cosmic egg or in the expanse of the sky beyond.

Whether on the surface of the earth, in the netherworld (Pātāla), or in the sky, or in water and wind; whether situated anywhere at all, or having taken their place in sacred fields (kṣetra), seats (pīṭha), and secondary seats (upapīṭha) and so forth—
the Goddesses are pleased by incense, lamps, and other offerings.
May those who are worshipped by the lords of heroes drink [the offering] according to the rite for the auspicious *sadāna* oblation;
with the mantra "Obeisance to the Yoginīs, Svāhā," one should offer to the Yoginīs using the thumb,
middle finger, and nose in the form of a vulva (*yoni*).

One should offer the oblation with the left thumb and ring finger while reciting the mantra: *liṃ dadyāt kṣāṃ kṣīṃ kṣūṃ kṣaiṃ kṣauṃ kṣaḥ huṃ sthānakṣetrapāla sarvakāmān pūraya svāhā*. [Then one should offer] *gāṃ gīṃ guṃ gaiṃ gauṃ gaḥ*.
With the mantra: "O Gaṇapati, bestower of boons, bring all people under my control;
accept this offering (*bali*) together with all ritual services, Svāhā!"—one should offer the *bali* to Gaṇeśa using the *añjali* gesture formed by curling the middle fingers.

Then, having filled [the vessel] and offered a handful of flowers with the mantra "samasta-prakaṭa," and having offered that handful of flowers, one should unite the wheel of the Khecarī-Śakti within oneself. Then, [perform] prāṇāyāma.
Having recollected the Ṛṣi and the other [limbs], one should satisfy the Lord upon the head with the nectar of the *arghya* offering;

then, having satisfied the Goddess in the heart three times, one should perform the worship of the Kumārīs and the worship of the Śaktis. [One should place] the vessel of the Goddess [and] the vessel of enjoyment...

Having scooped up the *traṃca* himself with another vessel, he should take it; other vessels as well should be given to those [disciples] according to their respective names. Then, he should recite the hymn of praise (*stotra*) to the Goddess.
"Having drunk the drops of pollen that are the meaning flowing from within the lotus-face of the Guru,
and having abandoned delusion, let the sovereign of practitioners meditate upon that beautiful woman like a bumblebee"— thus says the Āgama.
The seventh peacock-feather [of the crown] is the auspicious jewel of the image engraved by Macandra.

As for the hymn to the Goddess, it is according to the Vāmakeśvara and Kādima-tantras: Oṃ, [obeisance to her] whose form consists of Gaṇeśa, the planets, the lunar mansions, the Yoginīs, and the zodiac signs.
I bow to the Goddess Piṇī, who consists of mantra, who is Mātṛkā, and who takes the form of the sacred seats (pīṭhas).
I prostrate before the Great Goddess Mātṛkā, the Supreme Sovereign,
who brings about the destruction of the agitation caused by the surging waves of time.
When a man competes with the Sun, Garuḍa, the Moon, Cupid, Śiva, Fire, and Viṣṇu over even a single syllable or a single mora of this *Ṛiṇī* meter,
the three worlds become adorned by the moonlight of its syllables.
I bow to the Goddess Sarveśvarī, the Great Śrī Siddhamātṛkā.

(4) I bow to that Siddhamātṛkā, upon whose single syllable this triple world—from the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa) down to the shell of the universe—is strung like pearls upon a great thread. (5) She who is the eleventh [letter] of the foundation...

The universe, arising from the three corners of the solar seed-syllable (*ravīja*), extending from the Egg of Brahmā (*brahmāṇḍa*) to the outer shell (*kaṭāha*), is seen even today, firmly established from *a*, *ka*, *ca*, etc., up to *ṭa*. (6)
The eldest [goddess], whose letters belong to the *pa* class, who dwells in the cow, the mouth, the heart, the back, the hips, and the feet— her,
who is exalted by the letter *ī*. (7)

We bow down to the Great Goddess, who is the essence of essences, higher than the highest, whose nature is supreme bliss, even now [at whose birth... (8) Please note that the provided source text appears to be incomplete at the end. The translation reflects the available portion. (9) "Who is this? From where does he come?"— thus, by contemplating the nature of both form and formlessness, one should salute the Inexhaustible One who is accompanied by the hosts of gods, nāgas, and yakṣas.

The Goddess, whose form consists of the letters of the alphabet, is intensely radiant with the surging and overflowing currents of the *devīkula*; within her, by means of the sequential order of the classes (*varga*), the eight measures (*mātrā*) are established. (10)
One should worship her, the mistress of the eight great siddhis whose forms are the eight groups [of letters], the clever one who dwells within the venerable seat (śrīpīṭha) known as Kāmapūrṇaja.
"I bow to the illustrious Tripura, who is the treasury of wisdom"—
with these twelve verses, this hymn brings about all accomplishments;
it is a hymn to the Goddess in her indivisible form.
There is nothing beyond this; therefore, [follow] the Pañcamīstavarāja,
the Saubhāgyakavacarājarājeśvarīstava, and the Sundarīsahasranāma.

One should recite one of the hymns of praise. Now follows the method for the abbreviated worship (*saṃkocārcana*); this should be performed when there is a requirement for haste, and not otherwise, because of the hearing [in scripture] of misfortune [resulting from non-compliance]. In that regard, the abbreviation of the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) is as follows:

Having performed the placement of the seat (*thā-āsananyāsa*), the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*), the purification of the hands (*karaśuddhi*), and the placement of the sages and other [limbs] (*ṛṣyādinyāsa*), one should perform the placement of the Vaśinī group and the placement of the weapons (*āyudhanyāsa*);
this is one method. Another, however, [prescribes] the placement of the sages and others and the six-limbed placement...

"Thus [is] the contraction of worship: having performed [the rite] starting from the worship of the weapons (*āyudha-pūjā*) up to the worship of the Goddess (*devī-pūjā*), one should perform the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity.
This is the second [method], ending with the worship of the Goddesses of the Nine Yoginīs (*navayoni*) and so forth.

One should reflect upon what has been stated in the *Ādimata*, beginning with "the command" (*ājñā*) and so forth; furthermore, in the *Candrapīṭhāgama*, having worshipped the Goddess in the corner of the secret wheel (*rahasyacakra*) which serves as her weapon,
one should then lead her to the central corner and [worship her] again with ritual offerings (*upacāra*).

"Having worshipped and smelled [the offering], contemplate the light"—thus the contraction of the *homa* is as stated below; it is omitted here for fear of prolixity. Now, the definition of the mudrās: with both hands, one should clasp...

If one places the thumbs at the root joints of the little fingers as if forming a *liṅga*, this mudrā is considered the "invoker" (*āvāhinī*). If it is turned face down, it is considered the "establisher" (*sthāpinī*) mudrā; [if] the thumbs are raised...

The *muṣṭi* [mudrā], through the joining of the hands, is the *sannidhāpinī* (2). When the thumbs are inserted within, that same [mudrā] is considered the *saṃrodhinī*. When the pair of fists is turned upward, it is considered the *saṃmukhīkaraṇī* (3), [to be applied] upon the limbs of the deity in six parts.

The placement of the limbs (*nyāsa*) constitutes the ritual of sakalīkaraṇa. A fist formed with the right hand, with the index finger extended and pointing downward—this is known as the *avaguṇṭhana* mudrā;
when it is rotated all around and the hands are turned toward one another, it is so considered.

Furthermore, when the little fingers and ring fingers are joined together, and likewise the index and middle fingers [are joined], it is declared to be the *dhenu-mudrā*. By means of that, the best of practitioners should perform the consecration with nectar (*amṛtīkaraṇa*). [Then] the thumbs are interlaced with one another...
With the fingers of the hand extended, this is declared by the wise to be the Mahāmudrā for the purpose of bringing [the deity] near; one should employ this mudrā in the rite of invoking the deity,
as well as for agitation, driving away, attracting, subjugating, and maddening.
The nine mudrās known as Mahāṅkuśā, Khecarī, and Vījayoni have been described.
One should form them by turning the hands so that the two thumbs are clearly joined together, having placed the two index fingers inside the ring fingers.
O Maheśvarī, one should join the little fingers in the shape of a sesame seed at their respective places; this is known as the *trikhaṇḍā* [mudrā] for the rite of summoning Tripurā.
Having placed the middle fingers in the middle [of the palms], [one should place] the little fingers...
Having blocked the thumbs and formed the index fingers like a staff above the middle fingers at the nose—
this is the first mudrā, which causes universal agitation. In this very same mudrā, the two middle fingers are kept straight.

Now it is performed, O Supreme Goddess; this is considered the Sarvavidrāviṇī mudrā. With the middle and index fingers, and the little and ring fingers joined together in the form of a hook, placed in the middle, O Supreme Goddess—this [is it].

The *mākarṣiṇī* mudrā brings about the attraction of the three worlds. Having formed the two hands into the shape of a hollowed bowl (*puṭa*), the two index fingers are made into hooks; in this manner, they are turned in succession, with the middle fingers positioned below them in order.
By joining the little fingers, the index fingers, the nose-fingers (middle fingers), and so forth,
with all the thumbs pressed firmly together at their tips— O Supreme Lord, this mudrā is considered to bring everything under control. (4) [The hands] face each other.
Having joined the thumbs and middle fingers together at their centers, with the two little fingers straight and the two index fingers outside them in the shape of a staff,
and the two thumbs placed at the tips of the middle fingers— this is the Indrādi-mudrā.

The ring fingers of all women are not moistened; however, having placed the pair of her ring fingers below in the shape of a hook, one should apply the two index fingers in that same sequence. This is the Mahāṅkuśa [mudrā].

The Śāmudrā mudrā accomplishes all purposes and goals: O Mahādevī, having placed the left arm on the right side and the right arm on the left, and having fully interlaced the hands, [one should join] the little fingers and the ring fingers...
By what logic and in what sequence? O Maheśāna, when the two index fingers have been joined together and placed above all [the other fingers], one should also make the two thumbs straight;
this is named Sakhecarī.

The *mudrā* that is the most supreme among all the supreme is as follows: having turned the two hands so they are clearly visible, O Beloved, one should then form the pair of the index finger and thumb in the shape of a crescent moon;
then, the middle fingers should be pressed down by the little fingers.
One should likewise employ the middle fingers in a curved manner; all [the other fingers] should be placed below the ring fingers.
This is declared to be the Seed Mudrā (*bījamudrā*), which brings about all accomplishments. Having made the two middle fingers curved...
With the ring fingers placed upon the middle fingers,
and likewise the little fingers, all joined together and pressed by the thumbs— this is the first mudrā.

This is known as the *yonimudrā* (9). These mudrās of the Great Goddess Tripurā have been proclaimed; they should be employed at the time of the full moon according to their sequential application. These indeed are the nine mudrās.
Thus,
Rāmacandra, born from the jar in the ocean of the many Tantras,
has revealed this work for the benefit of the wise, like a streak of light from the eighth ray [of the sun].

The auspicious worship known as *Tnaprasūna* was mentioned there only incidentally; it was not explained in detail, nor was it relevant to the present subject. Therefore, O wise ones, pay heed to this completion of the ritual service (*saparyā*).
[Thus ends the eighth moonbeam, the Jewel of the Worship of the Blessed One, among the jewels of the worship of the Blessed One engraved by Āgamirāma Candrā at the command of Radevatā.
And this auspicious Jewel of the Worship of the Blessed One is completed.

176a) Om, salutations to Śiva. Having thus prostrated before the venerable Guru and visualized him as being well-pleased, one should receive his command from the mind and [proceed] from the *mūlādhāra*.
Upon the seat of the *śṛṅgāṭaka* within the triangular wheel situated in the pericarp of a four-petalled lotus with the color of molten gold,
one should contemplate the supreme power, Kuṇḍalinī, possessing the brilliance of a thousand rising suns.
She who resembles a flash of lightning, the mother of all mantras,
whose form consists of the fifty letters, who embodies the thirty-eight *kalās*,
the life-force of all living beings, the abode of the three abodes, and who is coiled like a serpent—
Having visualized her as facing upward, possessing three-and-a-half coils, the supreme deity above all gods,
endowed with consciousness through her innate name as instructed by the Guru, and having contemplated her sevenfold nature, [one should place] "Vaṃ" there upon the four petals.

Having worshipped [the petals] in clockwise order with the mantras "namaḥ śaṃ," "namaḥ ṣaṃ," and "namaḥ saṃ" on the petals, and with the root mantra (mūla) in the center, one should then move from lotus to lotus by means of the mantra "haṃ si" and proceed to the svādhiṣṭhāna.
Having brought that [energy] to the slightly red lotus at the base of the *liṅga*, one should worship there with the root mantra and on the petals with:
"Oṃ *vaṃ* namaḥ, *bhaṃ* namaḥ, *maṃ* namaḥ, *yaṃ* namaḥ, *raṃ* namaḥ, *laṃ* namaḥ. Then, one should worship in the center with the root mantra.
Then, having brought that [energy] to the blue-colored ten-petaled lotus at the navel by means of the maṇipūraka [vāyu], [one should recite]: ḍaṃ namaḥ, ḍhaṃ namaḥ,
ṇaṃ namaḥ, taṃ namaḥ, thaṃ namaḥ, daṃ namaḥ, dhaṃ namaḥ, naṃ namaḥ.

Having worshipped with *paṃ namaḥ* and *phaṃ namaḥ* on the petals and with the root mantra in the center, one should then lead her to the *anāhata-cakra* in the chest— a twelve-petaled lotus of pinkish-yellow color— and there [worship] with *kaṃ namaḥ* and *khaṃ*.

*Namaḥ gaṃ*, *namaḥ ghaṃ*, *namaḥ ṅaṃ*, *namaḥ caṃ*, *namaḥ chaṃ*, *namaḥ jaṃ*, *namaḥ jhaṃ*, *namaḥ ñaṃ*, *namaḥ ṭaṃ*, *namaḥ ṭhaṃ*— having thus worshipped on the petals and in the center with the root mantra, then [worship] at the throat.
Having visualized a sixteen-petaled lotus of smoky color in the *śuddhicakra*,
one should recite there: *aṃ namaḥ, āṃ namaḥ, iṃ namaḥ, ī namaḥ, uṃ namaḥ, ūṃ namaḥ,
ṛṃ namaḥ, ṝṃ namaḥ, ḷṃ namaḥ, ḹṃ namaḥ, aiṃ*.
Having worshipped with "Namaḥ aiṃ namaḥ," "Oṃ namaḥ," "Auṃ namaḥ," "Aṃ namaḥ," and "Aḥ namaḥ" upon the petals, and with the root mantra in the center,
one should then [worship] in the middle of the eyebrows at the Ājñā-cakra, the two-petaled lotus colored like lightning.
Having led it there, one should worship it with the root mantra between the two leaves saying "Haṃ Namaḥ Kṣaṃ Namaḥ," and then,
having caused it to reach the thousand-petaled lotus located at the *brahmarandhra*, [one should contemplate] the light in the form of a drop (*bindu*) therein.
Having attained oneness with Paramaśiva,
one should remain intent on hearing the *nāda* there for a *muhūrta*, contemplating dissolution; then,
like a lotus moving from one lotus to another, one should ascend everywhere with the realization, "I am that."
Being caused to ascend through the sequence beginning with the *ājñācakra*,

she is worshipped in each of those lotuses by those respective syllables; then, by means of the supreme nectar flowing therefrom, [she nourishes] each respective support, each respective element, and each respective...
Satisfying the respective presiding deities of those [centers] with the root-mantra,

and having brought [the energy] down to the *mūlādhāra*, one should establish it right there in its own place, the *mūlādhāra*. Thus, by the sequence of ascent and descent, one [should contemplate] the Supreme Power (*parā-śakti*).
Having meditated upon Kuṇḍalinī, one should perform the binding of the directions.
